The quality and taste were average, nothing special. For the price, I expected a premium product, but these mini-muffins fell short. Compared to other bakeries, the value is severely lacking. Overall, I would not recommend this bakery due to their outrageous pricing and tiny portions, making it a disappointing experience.

As I continued to enjoy my meal, I couldn't help but notice the generous portions that came with The Box Combo. The chicken strips were plentiful, and the fries, although not the most spectacular, were cooked to a perfect crisp. The Texas toast, as I mentioned earlier, was a highlight, and I found myself wishing I had ordered a few extra slices on the side. The cole slaw, while not the most creamy or flavorful I've had, provided a nice refreshing contrast to the richness of the chicken and fries.

The Cane's Sauce, which I was initially skeptical about, ended up being a pleasant surprise. It had a tangy, slightly sweet flavor that complemented the chicken nicely, and I found myself dipping my strips in it repeatedly. The sweet tea, as I mentioned earlier, was just sweet enough, and I appreciated the fact that it wasn't overpoweringly sugary.

One thing that impressed me about Raising Cane's was the evident care and attention that went into preparing my meal. Despite being a fast food joint, the staff seemed to take pride in their work, and the food was clearly made to order. The friendly service only added to the positive experience, and I appreciated the warm smile and welcoming demeanor of the staff member who handed me my order.

Overall, while Raising Cane's may not be the healthiest option, it's definitely a great choice for a quick, satisfying meal that's a step above the usual fast food fare. I would recommend it to anyone looking for a tasty, no-frills meal, and I'm looking forward to trying some of their other combos on my next visit. With its friendly staff, generous portions, and tasty food, Raising Cane's has won me over as a fan, and I'm excited to see what other delicious meals they have in store.

The atmosphere is lively and the staff is friendly. Overall, it's a wonderful spot to relax and enjoy a delicious meal with family or friends, and we're already looking forward to our next visit to try more of their tasty dishes and drinks.

Despite the charming atmosphere and appealing baked goods display, our overall experience at Urban Beans was disappointing. The lack of attention to detail, such as forgetting the whipped cream and serving lukewarm beverages, was surprising. The breakfast sandwiches, although generously sized, lacked flavor and texture, with untreated English muffins being a notable letdown. The delay in serving the sandwiches, which arrived after we had finished our drinks, added to the frustration. Given the moderate crowd, we expected more efficiency and care in the preparation and presentation of our order. While we appreciate the dog-friendly policy and the potential for a better experience with espresso and baked goods, our visit fell short of expectations. With some refinement in service, food quality, and cleanliness, Urban Beans could live up to its promising atmosphere and become a top choice for local breakfast and coffee enthusiasts. For now, however, we will explore other options.

I was extremely disappointed and frustrated with the experience, especially since I had confirmed the availability and price with my customer beforehand. The inefficiency of their ticket system and lack of actual stock on the floor is astounding. It's clear that Office Max is not equipped to handle electronics sales, and I would not recommend them to anyone looking for technology products. The significant price difference I found at Fry's Electronics only added to my disappointment, making me wonder how Office Max expects to compete in the electronics market. Overall, my experience was a waste of time and I will be taking my electronics business elsewhere.

The service was top-notch, with our server being attentive and knowledgeable about the menu. They made some great recommendations and ensured that our glasses were always full. The atmosphere was lively and fun, with a great mix of music and decor that added to the overall ambiance. We were impressed by the attention to detail and the care that the staff took to ensure that every aspect of our dining experience was enjoyable. Overall, we were thoroughly impressed with our visit to the Tip Top and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a great meal and a fun night out in Madison. With its unique menu offerings, extensive drink selection, and excellent service, the Tip Top is definitely a standout in the Madison dining scene. We can't wait to go back and try more of their delicious dishes!
Great service and delicious food, definitely a hidden gem, can't wait to bring my girlfriend and try more of their menu items.

As I sat in the audience, I couldn't help but feel a rush of excitement as the Blue Man Group took the stage. The energy was palpable, and it was clear that the performers were just as enthusiastic as the crowd. The show was a masterclass in creativity, with the group using everything from PVC pipes to LED lights to create an immersive experience. The "balls" segment, which I mentioned earlier, was a particular highlight - it was amazing to see how the group used these giant, bouncy orbs to create a sense of chaos and unpredictability.

One of the things that struck me about the show was the way the Blue Man Group interacted with the audience. Despite not speaking a word, they were able to connect with the crowd on a deep level, drawing people in and making them feel like they were part of the performance. The twinkie session, which I mentioned earlier, was a great example of this - it was hilarious to see the group use these innocent-looking snacks to create a sense of mischief and mayhem.

Of course, no review of the Blue Man Group would be complete without mentioning the finale, which was truly spectacular. The combination of fast music, flashing lights, and (of course) toilet paper created a sense of sensory overload that was exhilarating and exhausting at the same time. It was the perfect way to cap off an already incredible show, and it left me feeling energized and eager for more.

As I left the theater, I was grateful for the opportunity to meet the performers and take some photos. It was clear that they were passionate about what they did, and that they were dedicated to creating a unique and unforgettable experience for their audience. The live band, who played a crucial role in the show, were also on hand to chat and take photos - they were friendly and down-to-earth, and it was great to be able to show my appreciation for their hard work.

Overall, I would highly recommend the Blue Man Group to anyone looking for a fun and entertaining night out. The show is suitable for all ages, and it's a great way to experience something truly unique and creative. So if you get the chance to see them, don't hesitate - go for it, and get ready for an unforgettable experience!
Prices are reasonable, and the service is usually friendly, making it a decent option for casual dining or takeout, but nothing particularly stands out beyond their signature wings.

As I delved deeper into the world of La Gourmandine, I discovered that their attention to detail and commitment to using high-quality ingredients truly set them apart from other bakeries. The abricotine, with its delicate balance of flavors and textures, was a masterclass in French patisserie. The flaky, buttery croissant provided a perfect foundation for the rich pastry cream and sweet apricot jam, creating a delightful harmony of flavors that left me craving more.

The pain au chocolat, which my friend ordered, was equally impressive, with a generous amount of soft, velvety chocolate filling that complemented the crispy, golden-brown pastry perfectly. I was also impressed by the variety of options available, from classic croissants and danishes to more unique offerings like the abricotine. The presentation of each pastry was also noteworthy, with beautifully crafted designs and a clear attention to detail that made each item almost too pretty to eat.

Despite the initial wait in line, the service was friendly and efficient, with the staff happily answering questions and making recommendations. My suggestion to move the seating area outside still stands, as it would not only improve the flow of traffic inside the store but also provide a charming and inviting space for customers to enjoy their pastries. Overall, La Gourmandine is a must-visit destination for anyone looking for authentic, delicious French pastries in Pittsburgh, and I have no doubt that I will be returning again and again to sample more of their creations. With its exceptional quality, charming atmosphere, and dedication to traditional French baking techniques, La Gourmandine is a true gem in the heart of the city.

The burrito lacked the vibrant flavors I'm accustomed to. For the price, I expected more. Perhaps I'm spoiled by my weekly flea market treats, but I believe airports can offer better dining experiences. This meal was a letdown, and I wouldn't recommend it to fellow travelers seeking authentic Mexican cuisine.

to the Summerlin dining scene. The staff were friendly and attentive, but as I mentioned, the plethora of options and explanations for each pizza style and cooking method made the ordering process feel a bit overwhelming. Perhaps simplifying the menu or providing a clearer guide for newcomers would help streamline the experience. Despite the minor missteps, the quality of the ingredients and the creativity of the pizza offerings show promise. With a bit of refinement, particularly in their wine service and menu presentation, this pizzeria could easily become a top destination for pizza enthusiasts in the area. For now, it's a solid choice for those looking to try something new, and I'm interested to see how they continue to evolve and improve. Overall, a good start, and I'm excited to return and taste their progress.
Definitely will be back to sample their menu and enjoy more of their craft beers in a welcoming atmosphere always.

As we waited for our food, we took a glance around the restaurant and noticed the cozy atmosphere, complete with vintage decorations and a warm color scheme. The staff was friendly and attentive, checking in on us frequently to refill our drinks and ensure everything was to our liking. When our food arrived, we were impressed by the generous portion sizes and the presentation of our dishes. The BLT I ordered was cooked to perfection, with crispy bacon, fresh lettuce, and juicy tomato on toasted bread. My friend's club sandwich was equally impressive, with layers of turkey, bacon, lettuce, and tomato stacked high on three slices of bread.

The seasoned waffle fries were a nice touch, adding a satisfying crunch to our meals. We both agreed that the food was delicious and exceeded our expectations. The prices were also very reasonable, making it an excellent value for the quality and quantity of food we received. The bar special was an added bonus, and we took advantage of the $1.50 bottles of Bud Light Platinum to quench our thirst. Overall, our experience at Henry's was fantastic, and we're already looking forward to our next visit. The combination of great food, friendly service, and excellent value makes it a must-visit destination for anyone in the area. We're excited to try more of their menu items and explore the bar scene further. With its unassuming exterior and outstanding interior, Henry's is a hidden gem that's sure to become a favorite among locals and visitors alike.

As I continued to explore the buffet, I noticed that the service was attentive and friendly, with staff regularly refilling drinks and clearing tables. However, I did find it a bit odd that the crepe station was so heavily promoted, yet the chef was clearly overwhelmed with the demand. Perhaps having two or more chefs preparing crepes would help to reduce the wait time and improve the overall experience.

Despite the crepe station being a bit of a letdown, I was pleasantly surprised by the quality of the other dishes on offer. The mushrooms, as I mentioned earlier, were tasty, although a bit too saucy for my liking. I also enjoyed the variety of cheeses and breads available, which were perfect for snacking on while exploring the rest of the buffet.

One thing that did strike me as a bit odd was the lack of crab legs, which several other reviewers had mentioned as a highlight of the buffet. I'm not sure if they were just out of stock or if they're not a regular feature, but it was a bit disappointing not to see them.

On the other hand, the creme brulee was absolutely incredible, and I would highly recommend saving room for it. The combination of the creamy custard base and the perfectly caramelized sugar on top was absolute perfection. And the fact that the pastry chef had hidden away a few fruit tarts for special request was a lovely touch - it's always nice to feel like you're getting a little something extra.

The atmosphere of the buffet was also a major highlight, with the live birds flying around and the charming French-inspired decor making it feel like a real treat. I loved the option to sit "inside" or "outside", and the fact that the buffet was bustling but not too crowded made it feel like a really special experience.

If I were to offer any suggestions for improvement, it would be to consider adding more bathroom facilities - the single toilet was a bit of a bottleneck, and the line was quite long at times. It would also be nice to have a bit more clarity on what's included in the buffet price, as we were under the impression that mimosa was included, but it apparently wasn't.

Overall, while the buffet wasn't perfect, I did enjoy it more than my previous experience at Rio, and I would definitely consider returning in the future. Perhaps with a few tweaks to the crepe station and the bathroom situation, this buffet could really reach its full potential and become a must-visit destination for foodies in the area. As it stands, it's still a solid choice for a special occasion or a fun day out with friends, and I would recommend it to anyone looking for a unique and delicious dining experience.

The subpar service and food quality have finally driven us away. Despite its convenience, the constant mistakes and poor food preparation are unbearable. We're willing to trade a shorter drive for a better experience, hoping the next location will redeem the brand's reputation and serve fresher, more accurate orders with a side of good customer service.

Overall, the experience was average, with some hits and misses. The nostalgic factor is strong, but healthy it's not. If you're craving a guilty pleasure, this might satisfy. However, don't expect consistency in portion sizes. For the price, it's a decent option, but don't go in with high expectations for nutritional value or generous servings. It's a classic fast food joint with all the trimmings, including plenty of butter.

As I sat down to enjoy my meal, I couldn't help but appreciate the serene atmosphere and the fact that the food was indeed fresh and delicious. The use of local organic ingredients was evident in the flavors and textures of the dishes, and I appreciated the effort to support the local community. However, the prices did seem a bit steep, especially considering that the seating was exclusively outdoors. The country-store inside was a lovely touch, with its eclectic selection of handmade pastas, canned goods, and other specialty items. It was clear that the owners were passionate about promoting sustainable and artisanal practices. Despite the minor drawbacks, I would still recommend this spot to those looking for a unique and peaceful dining experience. The tree-lined drive and picturesque surroundings made for a lovely setting, and the ability to take a stroll with the baby or leave them in the stroller while socializing was a definite plus for young families. Overall, it's a great option for those seeking a healthy, farm-to-table meal in a relaxed and natural setting.

The fact that they tried to fix it after I complained is not enough to redeem their poor service. A good car wash and detailing should not require a customer to double-check their work. The initial lack of attention to detail and thoroughness is unacceptable, especially for the price paid. I expect a certain level of quality when paying $20 for a cleaning service. Unfortunately, this place fell short of my expectations. The experience left a bad taste in my mouth, and I would not recommend this place to anyone. Until they improve their quality control and attention to detail, I'll be taking my business elsewhere. One star is even generous, considering the subpar service I received.

Overall, I would recommend this place to those seeking traditional Japanese cuisine, but with managed expectations. The service was attentive and friendly, which added to the pleasant atmosphere. However, the prices might deter some customers from returning frequently. In comparison to other Japanese restaurants in the area, this one falls somewhere in the middle – not outstanding, but reliable. With a few tweaks to their menu, such as refining their fried dishes, they could potentially elevate their reputation. As it stands, it's a solid choice for a casual dinner, but not necessarily a destination restaurant.
is a bit steep for a casual morning coffee experience.

Overall, my experience was frustrating and unfulfilling. Despite the helpful customer service, the pressure to make a purchase and limited stock options made for a disappointing visit. I hope to find something worthy of the store credit in the future, but for now, I'm left with a negative impression. Unfortunately, this experience has deterred me from making future purchases, which is a shame given the initial excitement of receiving a gift from this store.

The atmosphere of the restaurant was cozy and inviting, with a modern decor that added to the overall charm. The service was also top-notch, with friendly and attentive staff who ensured that our glasses were always full. What truly impressed me, however, was the quality of the ingredients and the care with which each dish was prepared. The flavors were bold and well-balanced, and you could tell that the chefs were passionate about their craft. Overall, I would highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a delicious and authentic Italian dining experience. The prices were also very reasonable, making it a great value for the quality of food and service received.

I am extremely disappointed and frustrated with the way this situation was handled. The fact that they refused to take responsibility for their mistake and instead blamed me for returning my own clothes is unacceptable. The lack of accountability and poor customer service is shocking, especially considering the high price they charge for their services. I had expected a higher level of quality and attention to detail, but it seems that they are more interested in making a profit than in providing a reliable and trustworthy service.

The experience has left a sour taste in my mouth, and I would not recommend this business to anyone. The fact that they are willing to deny any wrongdoing and shift the blame to the customer is a clear indication of their priorities. I hope that others will learn from my experience and think twice before using their services. With so many other laundry options available, it's clear that this business is not worth the hassle and expense. Save yourself the trouble and take your business elsewhere. The convenience of their service is not worth the risk of losing your belongings or dealing with their uncooperative customer service team.

The lack of staffing is unacceptable, especially considering the consistent long lines. It's clear that the staff are doing their best, but they're being set up for failure. The limited parking and overcrowding only add to the frustration. I've tried to be patient and sympathetic, but it's getting to the point where I'd rather go out of my way to avoid this location. With so many other options available, it's surprising that this Post Office hasn't made any changes to improve their service. Until then, I'll be taking my business elsewhere.

Overall, our experience was disappointing, and the poor service overshadowed the affordability of the meal. The steak was overcooked, and the eggs were lukewarm, which further added to our frustration. Although the unique tabasco A1 sauce was a pleasant surprise, it wasn't enough to redeem the subpar food and service. For a 24-hour establishment, we expected more attention to detail and better coordination among the staff. Unfortunately, our visit fell short of expectations, and we would think twice before returning, despite the convenience of their hours and affordable prices. Perhaps they can improve with time and better training.

The breathtaking views of the city and surrounding mountains make every step worthwhile, with unique red rock formations and scenic overlooks to explore, leaving you feeling accomplished and eager to return.

The overall atmosphere of Blue Hound was lively and inviting, perfect for our group gathering. We were impressed by the extensive selection of appetizers, which offered something for everyone. From classic favorites to more unique options, each dish was expertly prepared and presented. Although our waiter seemed slightly put off by our appetizer-only order, the service remained attentive and courteous. The validated parking was a wonderful touch, adding to the overall value and convenience of our experience. We left feeling satisfied and already looking forward to our next visit, eager to explore more of the menu and enjoy the patio area.
Terribly expensive drinks and mediocre food make for a disappointing experience overall unfortunately always.

The service was friendly, but a bit slow. Our server seemed overwhelmed, but still managed to maintain a pleasant demeanor. Overall, it was a decent experience, but the happy hour limitations were a letdown. The Hangar 1 mandarin orange tini was a highlight, and I'd return for that alone. Perhaps a revisit on a less busy day would yield a more impressive experience, allowing me to fully appreciate their offerings.

We were expecting a more modern and luxurious stay, but unfortunately, the room's decor and size fell short of our expectations. The kitchen, although equipped with the essentials, was cramped and made cooking a challenge. The indoor pool was a nice touch, but it was often crowded and noisy. The fact that the resort is not located on the strip was also a drawback, as we had to rely on shuttles or taxis to get to the main attractions. Despite the friendly front desk staff and concierge, our overall experience was marred by the frustrating timeshare presentation and the resort's limitations. If you're looking for a hassle-free and modern stay, you might want to consider other options. However, if you're on a tight budget and don't mind the outdated decor and off-strip location, this resort might still be a decent choice. Just be prepared for the high-pressure sales pitch and plan your itinerary accordingly. Overall, our stay was average at best, and we would likely not return due to the timeshare presentation and the resort's overall lack of polish.

We thoroughly enjoyed our meals and the atmosphere was lively and inviting. The service was top-notch, with attentive waiters who ensured our glasses were always full. Although the prices were a bit steep, the quality and presentation of the dishes made it well worth the extra cost, leaving us with a wonderful dining experience.

As we finished our meal and prepared to leave, I couldn't help but feel a sense of disappointment. The atmosphere, although unique and visually appealing, didn't quite live up to my expectations. The food, while edible, was not impressive, and the prices seemed steep for the quality and quantity we received. I had been looking forward to trying this place for weeks, and the letdown was palpable.

Despite the subpar food, our waitress was friendly and attentive, making sure our drinks were always full and checking in on us regularly. However, even her excellent service couldn't make up for the shortcomings of the meal. As we left, I couldn't help but wonder if we had just caught them on a bad night or if this was the norm.

I've been to plenty of restaurants that have exceeded my expectations, and unfortunately, this one fell short. The Conquest Sandwich, while tasty, wasn't anything special, and the mushroom burger was a mess. The fries, although crispy and flavorful, couldn't redeem the soggy, falling-apart burger. It's a shame, really, because I had high hopes for this place.

Perhaps, as I mentioned earlier, I'll give it another try when I'm 21 and can experience the lounge area. Maybe the atmosphere and drinks will be enough to win me over. But for now, I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone looking for a satisfying, reasonably priced meal. There are plenty of other restaurants in the area that offer better food and value.

In retrospect, I think my expectations were inflated by the glowing reviews and photos. It's a good reminder to take online reviews with a grain of salt and not to get too caught up in the hype. Still, I'm always on the lookout for new restaurants to try, and I'm willing to give places a second chance. Maybe someday I'll return and have a better experience. Until then, I'll stick to other eateries that have proven themselves to be consistently delicious and worth the price.

Overall, despite a few minor hiccups with our entrees, the exceptional service and delightful appetizers made our dining experience truly memorable. The complimentary dessert was a lovely touch, and we appreciated the staff's attention to detail. While the kitchen may have been slightly off due to the busy Labor Day weekend, the server's prompt response to our concerns and willingness to make things right was impressive. We would definitely return to this restaurant and recommend it to others, hoping that on a less busy night, the entrees will live up to the high standards set by the appetizers and service.

The lack of cohesion and poorly executed transitions between acts made it feel like a disjointed mess. The attempts at humor and audience interaction fell flat, and the overall atmosphere was more cringeworthy than entertaining. I was expecting a high-energy, captivating show, but what I got was a dull, unimpressive experience. The talent of the individual performers was undeniable, but it was wasted on a lackluster production. I would not recommend this show to anyone, especially at the full price. Even at the discounted rate I paid, I felt ripped off. Unless they seriously revamp the show and address the numerous issues, I would advise others to skip it and explore the many other entertainment options Vegas has to offer. Overall, a disappointing and unmemorable experience.

The service was also quite friendly and attentive, with our server checking in on us regularly to refill our drinks and clear our plates. One thing that did stand out to me was the freshness of the ingredients, particularly the juices and the bacon, which were clearly made with high-quality components. However, as I mentioned earlier, the bagel and lox dish was a bit of a letdown in terms of presentation and value. Despite this, I would still recommend this spot to anyone looking for a convenient and delicious breakfast option while staying at the Saguaro. The atmosphere is certainly a major draw, and the staff's warm hospitality makes for a pleasant dining experience. If you're not too fussy about having a gourmet meal and just want something tasty and easy, then this place is a great choice. Overall, it's a solid option for a casual breakfast, and I would consider returning if I were in the area again.

The atmosphere is welcoming and relaxed, making it perfect for a casual night out with family or friends. The menu offers a great variety of options, and the prices are very reasonable. I've tried several items, and everything has been delicious and freshly prepared. The $6 burger deal is a steal, and the fish tacos are a must-try. Overall, I'm impressed with the quality of food and service, and I'll definitely be back to try more of their menu items. Highly recommended for a low-key, enjoyable dining experience.

The flavors and presentation are consistently impressive. Friendly staff and a cozy atmosphere make each visit enjoyable. I highly recommend Jun's for anyone seeking delicious, authentic Korean cuisine at an affordable price. Their commitment to quality and customer satisfaction is evident in every aspect of the dining experience, leaving me eager to return and try more of their offerings.

Overall, our recent dining experience at Mix was underwhelming, to say the least. The dishes lacked the finesse and attention to detail that we've come to expect from an Alain Ducasse establishment. The atmosphere, while once sleek and modern, now feels dated and over-the-top. Despite the knowledgeable and friendly wait staff, the subpar cuisine and exorbitant prices make it difficult for us to recommend Mix to others. Perhaps with a revamp of the menu and a refresh of the decor, Mix can regain its former glory, but until then, we'll be taking our business elsewhere. The locals seem to have caught on, as the restaurant was surprisingly empty on a weekend evening.

As a sushi aficionado, I was expecting a more authentic and flavorful experience, but unfortunately, Sushi Roku fell short. The lackluster sushi and overpriced special Toro were major letdowns. While my Chilean sea bass was cooked to perfection, the sauce was a misfire, and the pineapple flavor overpowered the truffle miso glaze. The mishap with my date's steak was disappointing, but I appreciate the prompt attention from the host and staff, who quickly rectified the issue.

Despite the culinary shortcomings, the service and decor at Sushi Roku were top-notch. Our waiter was attentive and knowledgeable, and the views of the strip were stunning. However, as I always say, good service and ambiance can only take you so far if the food doesn't deliver. If you're a sushi enthusiast like myself, you may want to explore other options. On the other hand, if you're in the mood for something more approachable and don't mind sacrificing some authenticity, Sushi Roku's rolls might be a safer bet. Ultimately, my experience was a mixed bag, and while I appreciate the efforts of the staff, I wouldn't rush back to Sushi Roku for their sushi. Perhaps with some tweaks to their menu and a focus on using fresher, higher-quality ingredients, they could elevate their game and become a contender in the competitive world of sushi. Until then, I'll be taking my sushi cravings elsewhere.
which makes it extremely convenient for a quick and satisfying meal anytime, highly recommend this local hidden gem always.

Insgesamt ist Arlt also eine gute Alternative zu den großen Elektronikmärkten, wenn man in Karlsruhe nach Computerteilen oder Zubehör sucht. Die Preise sind wie erwähnt günstiger und das Angebot ist umfangreich. Leider lässt der Service durch die langen Wartezeiten und den offensichtlichen Personalmangel zu wünschen übrig. Wenn man jedoch genau weiß, was man will und bereit ist, ein wenig zu warten oder die Ware im Voraus zu bestellen, kann man bei Arlt gute Geschäfte machen. Die Möglichkeit, die Ware im Internet zu bestellen und dann im Laden abzuholen, ist praktisch und die 3%-Ersparnis ist ein nettes Bonus. Es wäre jedoch schön, wenn Arlt das Personalproblem in den Griff bekäme, um den Einkaufsprozess noch angenehmer zu gestalten. Bis dahin bleibt Arlt eine gute Option für Computerkram in Karlsruhe, aber mit einigen Einschränkungen. Mit mehr Personal und verbessertem Service würde Arlt sicherlich zu einem noch besseren Anbieter werden und die fünf Sterne von mir erhalten. Bis dahin bleibt es bei vier Sternen, weil der Preis und das Angebot einfach zu gut sind, um nicht positiv hervorzuheben.

Overall, my experience at Bouchon was a mixed bag. While the food was undeniably delicious, the slow service really put a damper on the evening. I understand that handling a large group can be challenging, but it seemed like the staff was unprepared and disorganized. Despite the wait, the hot roasted pistachios and pain epi with butter were a lovely touch, and my salad and entree were both tasty and satisfying. It's clear that the kitchen is capable of producing high-quality dishes, but the front-of-house needs to step up their game. If you're a fan of raw oysters, it seems like Bouchon is the place to be, but for vegetarians, the options are limited. With some improvements to their service, I would consider returning to Bouchon, but for now, I would caution large groups to be prepared for a wait.

The atmosphere was cozy and intimate, with a rustic charm that added to the dining experience. Our server was attentive and knowledgeable, happy to answer questions about the menu and make recommendations. Overall, a fantastic evening with delicious food and excellent service, highly recommended for a night out.

The atmosphere of the Grapevine is also noteworthy, with a cozy and intimate setting that makes you feel like you're among friends. The decor is tasteful and understated, allowing the focus to remain on the wine and conversation. Whether you're a seasoned oenophile or just starting to explore the world of wine, the Grapevine is an ideal spot to learn and discover new favorites. The staff's passion for wine is infectious, and they're always happy to offer recommendations or share stories about the different varietals and vineyards they feature.

I've attended a few of their "Guest Bartender" charity events, and they're always a blast. The energy is lively, and it's great to see the community come together to support a good cause. The Grapevine's commitment to philanthropy is truly admirable, and it's clear that they're dedicated to making a positive impact in the area. Overall, I highly recommend the Grapevine to anyone looking for a unique and enjoyable wine experience. With its exceptional selection, knowledgeable staff, and community-focused spirit, it's a must-visit destination for wine lovers in the Baxter area. So grab a glass, pull up a stool, and get ready to indulge in the wonders of wine at the Grapevine!

In addition to the issues we experienced, the overall cleanliness of the room was also a concern. There were dust bunnies under the furniture and a general feeling of neglect. The new paint and pictures that had been added seemed like a superficial attempt to revamp the space, rather than a genuine effort to improve the quality of the accommodations.

The lack of attention to detail was further evident in the bathroom, where the spa tub, although a nice feature, was not properly cleaned. We found hair and soap scum from previous guests, which made us question the thoroughness of the housekeeping staff. The fact that the housekeeping lady had burst into our room without knocking earlier in our stay also made us wonder about the respect for guests' privacy.

Given the numerous problems we encountered, it's surprising that the manager, Dave, didn't seem more concerned about our experience. His dismissive attitude and lack of apology only added to our frustration. As we reflected on our stay, it became clear that the hotel's focus on rebranding and cosmetic updates had not translated to meaningful improvements in the quality of the rooms or the service provided.

Overall, our disappointing experience in room 1641 has left a lasting impression, and we would not recommend "The D" to others based on our stay. While the view from the room was pleasant, it was not enough to outweigh the numerous issues we encountered. Until the hotel addresses these problems and demonstrates a genuine commitment to providing a better experience for its guests, we would advise others to look elsewhere for their accommodations.

Perhaps the atmosphere will translate better during daylight hours, and the food and drink offerings will shine in a different light. The Papago orange blossom on tap was a highlight, and I appreciate the friendly staff's efforts to make us feel welcome. However, the extensive renovations and eclectic decor, while visually striking, feel like a mishmash of concepts rather than a cohesive vision. With some refinement and focus, this establishment could truly thrive and become a standout destination, rather than a confusing amalgam of styles and themes. I look forward to my next visit to see if they can find their footing.

...especially when you're expecting a hearty, satisfying meal. The lack of filling was really noticeable, and it felt like we were just eating a lot of bread with a hint of steak and cheese. The flavors were decent, but it wasn't enough to make up for the small portion size. My friend was surprised and disappointed by the change, as he had always enjoyed the philly steak Texas Style in the past. The atmosphere of the restaurant was lively and inviting, with plenty of TVs showing sports and a modern decor that added to the ambiance. However, the food was a letdown, and I hope that next time I visit, they will step up their game and provide a more generous serving. With a little improvement in the kitchen, this place could be a great spot to grab a bite, but for now, I'm not convinced.

The quality of the sushi is impressive, with fresh and delicious options to choose from. The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, making it a great spot for a night out. Overall, I highly recommend this place for anyone looking for a great all-you-can-eat sushi deal in Phoenix. The price is unbeatable and the service is excellent, making it a must-visit for sushi lovers.
Unbelievable customer service, completely ignored and disrespected as a customer, will not be returning to this location, extremely disappointing experience.

The service was absolutely appalling and the staff was extremely rude. We were treated like criminals, and it was clear they only cared about making a quick buck. The whole ordeal was humiliating and left a bad taste in our mouths. I would not recommend this place to my worst enemy, the promoters and staff are scams and thieves. Avoid at all costs.

Overall, I'm extremely satisfied with this buffet and have been going there for a while now. The variety of options is impressive, and the quality of the food is consistently good. I've tried many of the dishes, and they all taste authentic and delicious. The price point of $6.99 is unbeatable, making it an excellent option for families or large groups. The atmosphere is also pleasant, with a clean and spacious dining area. I appreciate the self-serve drink station, which eliminates the need to wait for refills. Whether you're in the mood for Chinese staples or something more unique, this buffet has something for everyone. I highly recommend giving it a try – you won't be disappointed! It's definitely my go-to spot for Chinese food.

Unfortunately, our experience with Thai Basil was a letdown. Despite the promising ratings and convenient location, the food failed to impress. The lack of heat in the dishes, particularly the Thai Basil Plate and Pad Thai, was surprising given our explicit request for "hot" spice level. As someone who frequently enjoys Thai cuisine, it was disappointing to find the flavors so subdued. The Pad Thai, in particular, was a disappointment, lacking the rich and complex flavors we've come to expect from this classic dish.

The fresh rolls, while having a good flavor, were also a bit of a mystery due to the unidentifiable crunchy ingredient. It would have been nice to have more options for protein, such as tofu or shrimp, to add some variety to the dish. Overall, while the Thai Basil Plate showed some promise, it wasn't enough to redeem the rest of the meal. Given the numerous excellent Thai restaurants in the Phoenix area that we've had the pleasure of trying, it's unlikely we'll be returning to Thai Basil. Perhaps they were just having an off day, but based on our experience, we wouldn't recommend it to fellow Thai food enthusiasts.

Overall, it was a great value and delicious meal. The atmosphere was lively and nostalgic, making for a pleasant dining experience. I would definitely return to try more of their specials and support their eco-friendly efforts in repurposing the old building. Service and food were both impressive.

The Italian Ice itself was refreshing on a hot day, but it lacked a distinct flavor profile that would set it apart from other similar establishments. The portion size was decent for the price, but the overall experience was just average. We didn't try any of their other offerings, such as the gelato or snacks, so maybe those are more impressive. However, based on our experience with the Italian Ice, we wouldn't go out of our way to recommend Joe's or make a special trip to return. Perhaps the crowds we've seen are due to the affordable prices or the novelty of the spot, but for us, it was just an unremarkable visit.

I've been to this place multiple times, and the lack of staff is a persistent issue. It's not just the wait times that are frustrating, but also the fact that they seem to be understaffed during peak hours. I've seen them juggling multiple customers at once, trying to handle phone calls, and dealing with walk-ins, all while maintaining a semblance of order. It's impressive, in a way, but also concerning. How can they expect to provide quality service when they're stretched so thin?

The fact that I had to wait 15-20 minutes on hold just to get an update on my glasses is unacceptable. And when I finally did get to speak to someone, they seemed put off by my inquiry. It was as if I was bothering them, rather than being a paying customer. The lack of communication and follow-through is a major issue here. If they can't even be bothered to call me when my glasses are ready, how can I trust them to get my prescription right?

The incident with the polarized coating on my sunglasses was the final straw. Not only did they damage my lenses, but they also seemed unconcerned about it. The lady who did the adjustment couldn't even see the problem, despite it being glaringly obvious. It took the manager to intervene and acknowledge the issue. And even then, it took them an inordinate amount of time to repair the lenses. I ended up getting a replacement pair online, which arrived in a fraction of the time it took them to fix my original pair.

The only redeeming quality of this place is the free adjustments. It's a nice perk, but it's not enough to outweigh the numerous drawbacks. If you value your time and want to avoid the frustration of dealing with an understaffed and disorganized optometrist, I would recommend taking your business (and your prescription) elsewhere.

In conclusion, while this place may be decent for eye exams and pricing, their customer service and follow-through are severely lacking. Unless they address the staffing issue and improve their communication, I would not recommend this place to anyone. It's just not worth the hassle and frustration. Get your exam, get your prescription, and take your business online or to a more reputable optometrist. Your time and sanity will thank you.

The unique selection and welcoming staff make it a must-visit. We appreciate the punch card rewards and look forward to trying more items. The store's quirky atmosphere and variety of sweets make it an excellent destination for special occasions and everyday treats, keeping us coming back for their distinctive goodies.

The experience was quite disappointing, especially considering the price point. It's unacceptable to serve an incomplete dish, especially one that's a direct copy of another restaurant's signature item. The fact that they didn't inform me of the missing ingredients beforehand or offer a discount is a clear indication of a lack of attention to detail and customer care. The offer of a cookie as compensation was also underwhelming, especially when compared to the $7.99 price tag of the salad. Overall, my experience was a letdown, and I would not recommend this place to anyone looking for a reliable and satisfying dining experience. With better options like Cowboy Ciao available, it's unlikely that I'll be returning to this establishment anytime soon. The Stetson salad at Cowboy Ciao is a game-changer, and I highly recommend giving it a try instead.

I'm extremely disappointed in the overall experience at this BBQ place. The fact that they can't even get the basics right, such as a decent sauce and tender meat, is shocking. The smokiness was overpowering and it felt like they were trying to hide the lack of flavor with a heavy-handed approach to smoking. The sides, as I mentioned, were mediocre at best and the absence of cornbread on the menu is a cardinal sin for any BBQ joint. The Hawaiian rolls were a pathetic substitute and lacked any real texture or taste. 

If you're looking for a genuine BBQ experience, keep looking. This place is a pale imitation of the real thing. The comparison to great BBQ places like those found in Texas or Dinosaur BBQ is almost laughable. Those places know how to do BBQ right, with rich, complex flavors and tender, fall-off-the-bone meat. In contrast, this place is a sad, sorry excuse for a BBQ restaurant. Save your money and your stomach, and avoid this place at all costs. One star is even too generous for this dump.

But if you're looking for a quality dining experience, keep looking. The lack of attention to detail and subpar food is not worth the savings. With so many exceptional restaurants in Las Vegas, it's surprising this place stays in business. Unless they revamp their menu and train their staff, I would not recommend wasting your time or money here. There are far better options available in the city.
Poor customer experience overall, will take my business elsewhere due to low quality food and unclean facilities.

As I sat there sipping my martini, I couldn't help but feel that Crave was trying to be something it's not. The ambiance was upscale, with modern decor and a trendy vibe, but the food and prices just didn't match. The edamame was cooked to perfection, but it was nothing out of the ordinary. The sushi rolls were fresh, but the flavors were not particularly unique or exciting. The jumbo shrimp was probably the highlight of the meal, but even that was not enough to justify the hefty price tag.

I understand that being located in a new and trendy area like Downtown Summerlin comes with a price, but I believe that Crave is taking advantage of its location to charge exorbitant prices. The menu is not particularly innovative or gourmet, and the portion sizes are not generous enough to warrant the high prices. As I mentioned earlier, I could get similar or even better quality food at other establishments like Ra or Sushi Roku without breaking the bank.

The service, however, was top-notch, and our server was attentive and friendly. The chef even came out to chat with us, which was a nice touch. But despite the great service, I just couldn't shake off the feeling that I was being overcharged for mediocre food. Perhaps Crave will revisit its pricing strategy and menu offerings to better reflect the quality and value of its dishes. Until then, I'm afraid I won't be returning anytime soon. With so many other great dining options in the area, I just don't see the value in paying premium prices for average food. Crave, you have a lot of potential, but you need to step up your game if you want to compete with the big players in the culinary scene.

The atmosphere, although not entirely electric, still maintained a certain allure, likely due to the venue's sleek design and impeccable upkeep. The transition from day to night seemed seamless, with the outdoor pool section and open-air Vegas strip view providing a unique backdrop for a nightclub experience. However, the crowd dynamics were somewhat off-putting, with a noticeable imbalance between the number of women and men, and a general lack of enthusiasm that is typically characteristic of a vibrant nightclub scene.

Despite the somewhat underwhelming experience, I appreciate the opportunity to have checked out the nightclub, especially considering its novelty. It will be interesting to see how the venue evolves over time, as it settles into its niche within the Las Vegas nightlife landscape. Perhaps with a more established crowd and a refined approach to programming, it will become a staple of the scene, offering a compelling alternative to more seasoned establishments like The Bank, where we ultimately ended up.

For now, I'm content to have had a sneak peek at this new addition to the Vegas nightlife roster, and I look forward to reassessing it during our next annual trip, when it will have had time to find its footing and potentially become a more integral part of the city's vibrant party scene. Until then, it remains a promising, if not yet fully realized, destination for those seeking a fresh take on the traditional nightclub experience.

The decor was modern and sleek, with plenty of natural light pouring in through the large windows. The outdoor seating area was also inviting, although I didn't get a chance to sit there. Our server was friendly and attentive, which was a plus. Despite the subpar food, the overall ambiance was enjoyable and made the experience slightly more bearable. Perhaps with a different dish or a revisit on a different day, my opinion might change. For now, I'd recommend this place for its atmosphere and service, but not necessarily for its brunch offerings.
Overall, it was a positive experience, and we would return to try their dine-in service, hoping the vegetable freshness improves, to fully appreciate their culinary offerings and cozy atmosphere.

The combination of flavors and textures is absolute perfection. The cheesesteak adds a nice savory element, while the ricotta cheese sauce brings a creamy richness. The onions, green peppers, and mushrooms add a fresh and earthy note to each bite. I'm not even kidding when I say this is the best pizza I've had in a long time. The service was also top-notch, with friendly staff and quick delivery. If you're a pizza lover like me, do yourself a favor and order this unique masterpiece - you won't regret it! It's a game-changer.

Overall, my experience at this place was average, and I wouldn't go out of my way to recommend it. The Chicken Philly sandwich was definitely a highlight, but the issue with my husband's order and the high prices were significant drawbacks. It's disappointing when you're looking forward to a hot, fresh meal and have to send it back because it's cold. The fact that they were able to remake it correctly is a plus, but it's not enough to outweigh the other issues. If they could work on their pricing and consistency with food temperature, I might consider giving them another try. As it stands, I would say that this place is just an okay option if you're in the mall and don't have other choices. There are likely better options available that offer similar or better quality food at more reasonable prices.

The variety of options was impressive, and the chefs were still willing to accommodate our orders even at such a late hour. The service was also top-notch, with friendly and attentive staff who ensured our glasses were always full and our plates were never empty. What really sets Hikari apart, though, is the value - for the price, you'd be hard-pressed to find a better all-you-can-eat sushi deal anywhere else. I've already recommended Hikari to all my friends and family, and I'm confident that it will become a staple for anyone looking for high-quality sushi in Vegas. Whether you're a sushi connoisseur or just looking for a unique dining experience, Hikari is definitely worth checking out. I'm already counting down the days until my next visit to Vegas, and Hikari will be at the top of my list.

The overall atmosphere of the restaurant was also lacking, with dim lighting that made it difficult to read the menu and a noisy ambiance that made conversation strained. The booth we were seated in was cramped and uncomfortable, with torn upholstery and a wobbly table. It's clear that the restaurant is in need of some serious renovations and updates. The food, as I mentioned, was a major letdown. The overcooked lamb was a travesty, and the lack of accompaniments such as rice or vegetables made the dish feel bare and overpriced. The inferno challenge, which my husband attempted, was also a disappointment. The fact that they charged us extra for a small dish of plain yogurt to help alleviate the spiciness was just salt in the wound. The service, as I mentioned earlier, was abysmal. Our waiters seemed completely uninterested in our table, and we were left to fend for ourselves for most of the meal. The fact that we had to get up and retrieve our own check and to-go boxes was just the final insult. Overall, our experience at this restaurant was a disaster from start to finish, and we will not be returning.

Overall, my experience at this location was underwhelming, especially given the upscale area it's situated in. The contrast to the other locations I frequent was stark, and I found myself wondering why this one hadn't received the same attention to detail and maintenance. As a regular user of the facilities, I expect a certain level of quality and cleanliness, which this location unfortunately failed to deliver. Unless significant renovations are made, I'll likely stick to my usual haunts, despite the convenience of this location's proximity to my workplace. Improvement is definitely needed here.

I was particularly impressed by the variety of options available, and my mom was thrilled to see some traditional dishes that she hadn't had in years. The har gow and siu mai were standout favorites, and the char siu bao was tender and flavorful. The prices were also very reasonable, especially considering the high quality of the food. I've been to other dim sum places where the dishes were overpriced and lacking in flavor, but this place truly delivers. The atmosphere was lively and bustling, with a warm and inviting decor that made us feel like we were in a authentic Chinese restaurant. Overall, I would highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a delicious and authentic dim sum experience. Don't let the negative reviews deter you - give it a try and see for yourself why it's a hidden gem.

The whole experience was frustrating and disorganized. With a lack of options and poor service, it's surprising they're still in business. The atmosphere was also underwhelming, with not enough TVs to accommodate sports fans. After waiting for what felt like an eternity, our food finally arrived, but the quality was subpar. For a brewery, you'd expect a decent selection of beers, but that wasn't the case here. Overall, our visit was a huge letdown, and we won't be returning. Two and a half hours of our time was wasted on poor service and mediocre food.

The lack of organization and attentiveness from the staff was staggering, and it seemed like they were all working independently without any cohesive system in place. Our server, who finally took our orders, seemed overwhelmed and took a while to return with our food. The chili cheese fries I ordered were a major letdown, and the "volcano" chili was a misnomer - it was bland and had an odd sweetness to it, which I can only assume was from the BBQ sauce. The portion size was also smaller than expected, especially considering the price. My friend's beer experience was also a disappointment, and the fact that they didn't have a working tap system was concerning. Overall, the combination of poor service, subpar food, and lack of attention to detail made for a thoroughly unenjoyable experience. I would not recommend this place to anyone, unless they're looking for a disappointing and overpriced meal. With so many other great options available, it's hard to see why anyone would choose to return to this establishment. Needless to say, my friend and I will be taking our business (and our appetites) elsewhere.

Despite the wait, the Parmesan truffle fries and Ronin burger were standout dishes, showcasing the kitchen's potential. However, the inconsistent cooking of my burger, being too pink for a medium-well order, was a letdown. This mistake has happened to me before at this location, which raises concerns about quality control. Furthermore, the forgetfulness of my husband's tea order added to the frustration. The ambiance of the restaurant is certainly a strong point, but it's not enough to make up for the subpar service and kitchen mishaps. With some improvements in these areas, this restaurant could truly excel.

The service is also top-notch, friendly staff and a cozy atmosphere make it a perfect spot for dates or gatherings, we always leave feeling satisfied and already planning our next visit, definitely a favorite restaurant of ours, can't wait to try more of their creative dishes!

As I explored the store, I was impressed by the wide selection of international products, from exotic spices to artisanal cheeses. The store's commitment to showcasing local and sustainable products is truly commendable. I was also delighted to find a variety of ready-to-eat options, including a salad bar and a hot food counter, which made for a quick and delicious lunch.

The store's atmosphere was lively and welcoming, with upbeat music playing in the background and the aroma of freshly baked bread wafting through the air. I appreciated the fact that the store had a dedicated section for dietary restrictions, making it easy for customers with special needs to find suitable options.

One thing that sets this world market apart from others is its community-oriented approach. The store hosts various events and workshops, from cooking classes to wine tastings, which fosters a sense of connection among customers and staff. Overall, my first visit to this particular world market was a resounding success, and I'm eager to return and continue exploring the many wonders it has to offer. With its unique blend of global cuisine, eclectic products, and welcoming atmosphere, this store is sure to become a staple in my weekly shopping routine.

Extremely unhelpful and unprofessional experience. The lack of electronic fingerprinting capabilities is surprising, given the name "Live Scan Las Vegas". The long processing time and poor customer service make it not worth the hassle. Burton's studio is a much better option, with friendly staff and efficient services. Save yourself the frustration and avoid this place altogether, opting for a more reliable and courteous alternative instead.

The lack of authenticity and overreliance on spices is truly disappointing. As someone who has a deep appreciation for Mexican cuisine, it's disheartening to see a restaurant like Mad Mex perpetuating a watered-down, unbalanced representation of Tex-Mex. The fact that the wings, typically an American pub staple, were the highlight of the meal speaks volumes about the kitchen's priorities. The Carnitas, which had potential, was ultimately overpowered by an excessive amount of spice, leaving me wondering if the chef has ever actually tasted the nuances of traditional Mexican cooking. With so many excellent Mexican and Tex-Mex restaurants out there, it's puzzling that Mad Mex continues to attract customers. Perhaps, as I mentioned earlier, the dim lighting and liberal drink pours are enough to distract from the subpar food, but for those seeking a genuine culinary experience, there are far better options available. Overall, my experience at Mad Mex was a letdown, and I would not recommend it to anyone seeking authentic, well-crafted Mexican or Tex-Mex cuisine.

Prices were reasonable, and the cozy atmosphere added to our enjoyment. We would definitely return to try more of their creative dishes and appreciate the bring-your-own wine policy, making for a lovely evening out in the Rue Duluth neighborhood. Highly recommended for a delicious meal.

As I continued my stay, I was disappointed to find that the resort's lack of amenities and subpar services were not the only issues. The rooms, although touted as luxurious, were in dire need of renovation. The furniture was outdated, the carpets were stained, and the air conditioning unit was loud and inefficient. The kitchen, which was supposed to be a major selling point, was a letdown. The appliances were old and difficult to use, and the lack of basic cooking utensils and supplies made it difficult to prepare even the simplest of meals.

The resort's location, which I had initially thought would be a plus, turned out to be a major drawback. The $30 cab ride to The Strip was a significant expense, and the shuttle service, which was supposed to be a convenient alternative, was unreliable and restrictive. The fact that it only ran from 10 am to midnight and did not allow bags or luggage made it virtually useless for anyone attending conventions or events.

The Wi-Fi situation was also a major inconvenience. Having to pay for Wi-Fi in the rooms was bad enough, but the fact that it was only free in the lobby made it difficult to get any work done or stay connected with family and friends. And don't even get me started on the lack of a restaurant on the premises. Having to venture out to find food or buy groceries was a hassle, especially considering the resort's isolated location.

But the final straw was the cockroaches. I had never seen so many in my life, and they were everywhere - in the rooms, around the pool, and even in the lobby. It was disgusting and made me question the resort's cleanliness and maintenance. The fact that pest control was not included in the yearly dues was appalling, and it made me wonder what else the resort was skimping on.

As I checked out and left the resort, I couldn't help but feel relieved to be leaving such a disappointing and overpriced experience behind. The resort's lack of amenities, subpar services, and numerous issues made it a place I would never recommend to anyone. In fact, I would advise people to steer clear of it altogether. With so many other great options in Las Vegas, there's no reason to settle for a mediocre resort like this one. Save your money and your sanity, and choose a different resort for your next vacation. Trust me, you won't regret it.

In conclusion, my experience at this resort was a disaster from start to finish. The lack of amenities, the poor location, and the numerous issues with the rooms and services made it a place I would never want to visit again. As an RCI member, I expect a certain level of quality and service, and this resort fell far short of those expectations. I hope that in the future, the resort will take steps to address these issues and provide a better experience for its guests. But until then, I would not recommend it to anyone.

I'm extremely disappointed in the decline of Bally's, a hotel I've always held in high regard. The issues we encountered during our recent stay were not only frustrating but also unacceptable. Firstly, the people movers being down again was a huge inconvenience, especially considering our mobility issues. After a long day of walking around the convention, we rely on these to get around the hotel. 

The upgrade to our usual suite was a nice gesture, but finding dirty diapers by the window was absolutely appalling. The $30 dining credit offered as compensation was a mere token and didn't come close to making up for the disgust and discomfort we felt. On a more positive note, the roulette dealer was exceptional and provided top-notch service. The valet driver, Regina, was also outstanding and remembered our names after a year, which was a lovely personal touch.

However, my main gripe remains the people movers. I understand that they may be turned off near the entrance to encourage people to sit at machines, but this is a poor excuse for a hotel that claims to cater to its guests' needs. I implore the management to take our complaints seriously and take immediate action to address these issues. Until then, I'm afraid Bally's will continue to lose its loyal customers.

The BARBIE slider was cooked to perfection, with a generous patty, crispy bacon, and melted cheese all coming together in harmony. The portion was massive, and I appreciated the generous serving. Despite the disappointment with the fries, the overall experience was exceptional. The staff was friendly and apologetic about the fry situation, which showed they care about their customers. I'm already planning my next visit to try more of their menu items, including those elusive peanut oil fries. With its unique flavors and generous portions, this truck has won me over, and I'm excited to see what the future holds for this Vegas gem.

for an unforgettable dining experience. The teppanyaki grill added a fun twist to our evening. Margarita's recommendations were spot on, and Tim's culinary skills impressed us. The filet mignon and lobster tail were cooked to perfection. We left feeling satisfied and already looking forward to our next visit. Benihana exceeded our expectations, and we highly recommend it to anyone seeking a unique and delicious meal.

I'm extremely disappointed in the way they handled my payment. The overall experience was enjoyable, with a great selection of music and a lively atmosphere, but the billing issue has left a sour taste. The multiple rooms and outdoor area were definite perks, and the bartender's generosity was appreciated. However, the alleged theft has overshadowed the positives. I hope the establishment takes steps to address this issue and prevent it from happening to others. Until then, I would advise patrons to closely monitor their transactions. A fun night out should not be marred by dishonest business practices.

The lack of transparency and inconsistent information is not only frustrating but also a waste of time. I've had to reschedule multiple times due to their limited hours and unavailability of staff. The fact that they don't have a nurse on site regularly is unacceptable, especially for a clinic that offers shots and other medical services. The inconvenience and poor communication make it clear that this clinic is not patient-centered. With so many other options available, I would strongly advise against visiting this clinic. Their inflexible schedule and subpar service make them a last resort, at best.

The atmosphere was lovely, with elegant decor and a nice view, but the poor service really overshadowed our experience. It's a shame, because I was really looking forward to trying their French cuisine. Instead, we left feeling frustrated and undervalued as customers. The fact that our waitress became defensive and argumentative when we pointed out the mistake was completely unacceptable. As a customer, you expect to be treated with respect and courtesy, especially in a high-end establishment like this. Unfortunately, our visit fell far short of expectations, and I would caution others to be aware of the potential for poor service when visiting this restaurant. Overall, a disappointing experience that I won't soon forget.

I've been to Big Wong several times, and each visit has been a delightful experience. The service is always friendly and prompt, with the staff eager to recommend their favorite dishes. The atmosphere is casual and no-frills, which suits the affordable prices and generous portions. The crispy shrimp wontons are a must-try, with a perfect balance of crunch and flavor. The salt and pepper wings are also a highlight, with a spicy kick that will leave you wanting more. The chicken curry is rich and creamy, with tender chunks of chicken that fall apart easily. With such a vast menu at an unbeatable price point, Big Wong is an excellent choice for a quick and satisfying meal. Whether you're in the mood for something classic or adventurous, Big Wong has something for everyone. Be sure to call ahead for take-out, and enjoy your delicious and affordable meal on-the-go.

The overall experience was disappointing and the food quality was subpar. I expected more from this establishment, but unfortunately, it failed to meet my expectations, leaving a bad taste and unpleasant after-effects. Needless to say, I won't be returning anytime soon.

The atmosphere was lively and upscale, with a pleasant decor that added to the overall dining experience. Our server was attentive and friendly, ensuring that our drinks were always filled and clearing our plates promptly. The variety of options was impressive, and we appreciated the creativity that went into crafting each dish. The small portions allowed us to try a little bit of everything, and we were surprised by how much we enjoyed some of the unique flavor combinations. Overall, we were thoroughly impressed with the quality and value of the buffet, and we can't wait to come back and try more of their innovative dishes. The price was very reasonable, especially considering the high quality of the food and the generous selection.

Despite the waitress's behavior, we managed to enjoy our meal and each other's company. The portions were generous, and the prices were reasonable, making it a good value for the quality of food we received. However, the experience was somewhat marred by the waitress's consistent attitude and lack of warmth. It's understandable to have an off day, but if this is a regular occurrence, it may be worth the restaurant's attention to improve their overall customer service.

The atmosphere of the restaurant was pleasant, with a traditional Chinese decor and a clean, well-maintained dining area. The Lazy Susan at our table was a nice touch, even if we didn't end up sharing our food as much as we had hoped. Overall, while the food was good and the prices were fair, the service left a bit to be desired. If you're looking for a reliable Chinese food option and don't mind a potentially gruff server, this might be a good choice. But if you're prioritizing excellent customer service, you might want to look elsewhere. With a bit more attention to training their staff, this restaurant could easily become a top choice for Chinese food in the area.

Overall, Roman Candle is a fantastic spot for casual dining, and I appreciate the efforts to incorporate local flavors and ingredients. The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, making it perfect for a night out with friends or a family dinner. With its unique pizza offerings and excellent supporting menu items, Roman Candle has become a staple in my dining routine, and I highly recommend it to anyone in the area looking for a delicious meal.

I also appreciate the convenience of being able to filter by size, style, and brand when shopping online, which makes it much easier to find what I'm looking for. In contrast, browsing through the racks at this store can be overwhelming, especially when everything is jumbled together. I've found that even when I do stumble upon a brand or style I like, the sizing can be inconsistent, which adds to the frustration.

Another issue I've encountered is the quality of the items. While the prices may be low, I've noticed that some of the clothes can be quite worn or faded, even if they're still in decent condition. As a parent, I want to make sure my baby's clothes are not only cute but also comfortable and durable. Unfortunately, I haven't always been impressed with the quality of the items I've found at this store.

Overall, while I understand the appeal of thrift shopping and the potential to find hidden gems, I just haven't had the best experience at this particular store. The disorganization, limited selection of brands I like, and inconsistent quality have all contributed to my decision to shop elsewhere. For me, the convenience and reliability of online shopping outweigh the potential savings of thrift shopping, at least when it comes to baby clothes.

Extremely disappointed and frustrated with the service and attention to detail. The mistake was not only inconvenient but also a dietary concern. Will not be returning to this location anytime soon, expecting better quality control and customer satisfaction from a reputable establishment like this. Totally unacceptable experience overall.

I must say that my experience with Ikea has been a mixed bag. On one hand, I was pleased with the service I received from Mark, the salesperson who helped me find the perfect bedroom furniture. He was knowledgeable, friendly, and made sure I had everything I needed. However, the problems I encountered after leaving the store were frustrating and disappointing. The missing hardware for the slats was a significant issue, and the lack of follow-up from Kim was unacceptable.

I was shocked that the call center in Maryland was unable to assist me in a timely manner, and the options they presented were not feasible for me. Having to drive 234 miles back to the store or wait a week for the missing items to be shipped was not a reasonable solution. It was only when I contacted the corporate office and spoke with Felicia that I received the kind of service I expected from Ikea. She listened to my concerns, empathized with my situation, and offered to help resolve the issue promptly. I appreciate her efforts, and I hope that the parts will arrive within the promised timeframe. If they do, I will reconsider my review and rating. However, if the issue is not resolved satisfactorily, I will stand by my original assessment.

The prices were also very reasonable, making it an excellent value for the quality and quantity of food. I've already recommended this place to friends and family, and I'm excited to return and try more of their menu items. The staff were attentive and knowledgeable, happy to answer questions and make suggestions. Overall, my impulsive stop turned into a fantastic dining experience that I won't soon forget. I'm looking forward to enjoying more of their delicious po'boys and beignets when I return to New Orleans next month. It's definitely a must-visit destination for any food lover.

The pastie was delicious and filling, a great start to the day. Despite the small space, the service was friendly and efficient. I was distracted by the drumset and the mysterious Myles Teddywedger, whose apparent passing added a somber note to my visit. Overall, I'd recommend this quirky spot for a tasty breakfast treat, but be prepared for a cramped and eclectic experience.

The lack of attention to detail and care in the preparation of our meals was truly disappointing. As a local, I expect more from a renowned restaurant like Spago. The atmosphere, which was once lively and inviting, now feels like a tired, overpriced tourist trap. Our server seemed put off by our presence, and the overall service was slow and inattentive. In contrast, Wolfgang Puck at Crystals offers a far superior dining experience, with fresh, expertly prepared dishes and a warm, welcoming staff. The 20% discount for locals is just the icing on the cake. Unless Spago makes significant changes, I would not recommend it to anyone, local or tourist alike. There are far better options available, and I will be taking my business elsewhere from now on.

As I continue to reflect on our experience living in this complex, I am reminded of the countless times we've had to deal with the incompetence of the staff and management. The lack of accountability and transparency is staggering. It's like they're not even trying to provide a decent living environment for their tenants. The constant excuses and blame-shifting are exhausting. When we first moved in, we were promised a certain level of service and amenities, but it's clear that those promises were nothing more than empty words.

The condition of the grounds and common areas is a perfect reflection of the management's priorities. The dog waste, cigarette butts, and trash are not only an eyesore, but they also create a health hazard. The fact that they can't even be bothered to clean up after themselves is appalling. And don't even get me started on the pool. The excuse that tenants spilling beer is causing the pool to turn green is laughable. It's clear that they're not properly maintaining the pool, and it's a shame that we're paying for a amenity that we can't even use.

The scorpion and bug problem is also a major concern. As a parent, it's terrifying to think that my infant daughter could be at risk of being stung or bitten. The fact that the office staff laughed at my concerns is despicable. It's not funny, it's not trivial, and it's not something that should be taken lightly. The fact that they give me grief when I ask for the bug guy to come spray our apartment is just another example of their incompetence.

The financial issues we've experienced are also a major red flag. Being overcharged $450 is a significant amount of money, and the fact that the office staff couldn't help me resolve the issue is unacceptable. The fact that they told me to just pay the amount and any extra would go towards my next month's rent is not only unhelpful, but it's also unprofessional. And the fact that they threatened me with late fees when their website was down and they couldn't even tell me how much I owed is just ridiculous.

As I look back on our experience, I am reminded of the countless times we've had to deal with the stress and frustration of living in this complex. It's not just the big things, it's the little things too. The fact that they can't even get the basics right, like providing a clean and safe living environment, is a clear indication that they're not interested in being a good landlord. They're only interested in collecting our rent and providing the bare minimum.

To anyone considering moving to this complex, I would strongly advise against it. The little extra you might pay to live somewhere else is worth it. This place is a nightmare, and it's not worth the stress and frustration. I hope that the management and staff will take our experience and the experiences of others to heart and make some serious changes. But until then, I would not recommend this complex to my worst enemy.

In conclusion, our experience living in this complex has been a disaster. The staff and management are incompetent, the grounds and common areas are a mess, and the financial issues are a major concern. The scorpion and bug problem is a serious health hazard, and the fact that they don't take it seriously is terrifying. I hope that our review will serve as a warning to others and that they will take our experience into consideration when deciding where to live. Don't make the same mistake we did, spend the little extra and go elsewhere. This place is a shit hole, and it's not worth your time or money.

The atmosphere is lively and inviting, making it perfect for a casual evening out with friends. While the blue wasabi is a unique touch, it's not a game-changer. Overall, the experience was pleasant, but not exceptional. The consistently good food and nice ambiance make it a reliable choice for happy hour or dinner. However, don't expect to be blown away by anything extraordinary. It's a solid, middle-of-the-road sushi spot that gets the job done, but doesn't particularly stand out from the crowd.
