The service was also top-notch, with friendly and attentive staff who ensured our glasses were always full. However, the prices were a bit steep for the quality of sushi we received. Overall, Stingray seems to be more of a trendy spot to grab a drink and socialize rather than a premier sushi destination. That being said, I would still recommend it for a night out with friends or a date, as the ambiance and cocktails are certainly worth experiencing. With a few tweaks to their sushi menu, Stingray could easily become a 4-star establishment in my book.

I was left waiting and hungry, relying on their assurance that my order was on its way. Unfortunately, it never arrived, and I was forced to go without dinner. The lack of honesty and communication from Tandoor is disappointing, especially given my frequent orders from them. I hope they will take steps to improve their customer service and delivery process to prevent similar experiences in the future. This incident has left a sour taste, making me reconsider my loyalty to their restaurant.

I'm extremely disappointed in this decision, as it will likely lead to longer wait times and more frustration for customers. The removal of self-checkout lanes seems like a step backwards, especially when most stores are embracing technology to improve the shopping experience. I hope the management will reconsider their decision and reinstate the self-checkout lanes to better serve their customers. Until then, I'll be exploring other grocery options that prioritize convenience and efficiency. The loss of self-checkout is a significant inconvenience that may ultimately drive me away from this store.

The atmosphere was lively and the staff were attentive, ensuring our group had everything we needed. The prices were very reasonable, making it an excellent value for the quality of food and service received. Overall, I'm glad I had the opportunity to revisit Sierra Gold and I would definitely recommend it to others looking for a great casual dining experience with a fun atmosphere. I'll be back sooner rather than later to try more of their menu items.

As I reflect on our disastrous stay, I am still fuming about the sheer lack of attention to detail and customer care displayed by the hotel staff. It's astonishing that a establishment that claims to be a hotel can't even manage to assign unique room keys to its guests. The fact that another couple was able to enter our room with their key while I was changing is not only unsettling but also a serious breach of security and privacy.

The noise levels throughout our stay were also unbearable. The constant disruptions from the loud talking and screaming in the hallway and parking lot made it impossible for us to get a good night's sleep. And when we finally worked up the courage to call the lobby to complain, the staff seemed completely unbothered and took their sweet time to address the issue. It's clear that the hotel's priority is not the comfort and well-being of its guests.

The hotel's design and layout are also poorly thought out. The extremely long hallways and limited number of floors make it feel more like a budget motel than a legitimate hotel. And the fact that the doors and windows do nothing to soundproof the rooms means that you can hear every conversation, footstep, and door slam from the surrounding areas.

The subpar breakfast selection and overcrowded pool area only added to our disappointment. The gym, which I was looking forward to using, was a joke - with only a few pieces of equipment and a plethora of mirrors that made it feel more like a narcissist's playground than a legitimate fitness center.

In conclusion, our experience at this hotel was an unmitigated disaster. The combination of security breaches, noise disruptions, poor design, and subpar amenities makes it a place that I would not recommend to my worst enemy. If you value your sanity, your safety, and your comfort, stay far, far away from this dump. There are plenty of other hotels in the area that actually prioritize their guests' needs and provide a decent night's stay. Don't make the same mistake we did - choose somewhere else.

As I sat at my table, I couldn't help but notice the inconsistencies in the service. Our server seemed overwhelmed, taking ages to take our orders and forgetting one of our appetizers altogether. When I politely asked for a refill on my drink, I was met with a sigh and a long wait. The food, on the other hand, was a different story. The dishes were creative and flavorful, with fresh ingredients and interesting combinations. The presentation was also impressive, with garnishes and plating that added to the overall appeal.

However, the high prices and slow service made it difficult to fully enjoy the meal. I felt like I was being nickel-and-dimed, with extra charges for everything from bread to sides. The ambience, while pleasant, wasn't enough to make up for the shortcomings in service and value. The restaurant's atmosphere was modern and sleek, with a cozy patio area and a bustling bar scene. But when the bill arrived, I was shocked by the total, and the lack of attention from our server made it feel like they were just trying to get us out the door.

Overall, my experience was a mixed bag. While the food showed promise, the service and prices were major drawbacks. With a little attention to detail and a focus on customer satisfaction, this restaurant could reach its full potential. Until then, I would caution potential diners to be aware of the wait times and high prices, and to manage their expectations accordingly. Perhaps with some tweaks to their service model and pricing strategy, this restaurant can become a truly exceptional dining experience. But for now, it falls short of being a top recommendation.

I'm still fuming about the incident with my cousin, but I'll try to give a fair review of the rest of the night. As I mentioned earlier, DJ Exodus was amazing, and the music was definitely the highlight of the evening. The table service was also top-notch, and our personal security guard was friendly and attentive. The drinks were pricey, but that's to be expected at a club like this. The VIP experience was worth it, though, as we were able to skip the long lines and get priority access to the bar.

The club itself was nicely decorated, and the atmosphere was electric. The crowd was lively, but not too rowdy, and everyone seemed to be having a good time. The dance floor was packed, but we had a great view of the DJ from our table, and we were able to dance and enjoy the music without feeling too crowded.

Despite the incident with my cousin, the rest of the staff at the Moon were friendly and helpful. Our server was attentive and made sure we had everything we needed, and the bartender was knowledgeable and made some great recommendations.

However, the security team needs some serious retraining. I understand that they have a job to do, but there's no excuse for the way they treated my cousin. He was not causing a scene or disturbing anyone, and there was no reason for them to escalate the situation like they did. It's unacceptable to put someone in cuffs and drag them across the street, especially when they're a paying customer who's just trying to have a good time.

Overall, I would still recommend the Moon to others, but with some caveats. If you're looking for a great DJ and a lively atmosphere, this is definitely the place to go. Just be aware that the security team can be a bit overzealous, and be prepared for some long lines and pricey drinks. And if you're planning to get a table, make sure you're aware of the rules and regulations, and don't be afraid to speak up if you feel like you're being treated unfairly.

In the end, my birthday celebration was still a success, despite the incident with my cousin. The music and the atmosphere at the Moon were amazing, and I had a great time dancing and celebrating with my friends. I just hope that the Moon will take steps to address the issues with their security team, so that others can have a positive experience without any problems.

I appreciate the restraint of their condensed menu, as it allows for a more curated experience without overwhelming options. The atmosphere, although not particularly impressive, is cozy and inviting, making it an ideal spot for a late-night craving. Despite the service being virtually non-existent, the food arrived promptly, which suggests that the kitchen is well-organized. While it may not surpass my beloved Orchid Garden, Harbor Palace has earned a spot as a worthy alternative, particularly for those seeking a more subdued dim sum experience. With its extended hours and fair prices, I foresee myself returning to sample more of their offerings, perhaps becoming a regular at this unlikely 4th of July discovery. The unique experience has left a lasting impression, making me eager to explore more.

In addition to their unique rolls and special dishes, I was also impressed by the freshness and quality of their ingredients. The fish was always flavorful and tender, and the rice was cooked to perfection. The atmosphere of the restaurant was also noteworthy, with a modern and sleek decor that added to the overall dining experience. The staff were attentive and knowledgeable, happy to answer any questions I had about the menu or make recommendations. One thing that did stand out to me was the pace of service, which was well-balanced - not too slow, but not too rushed either. This allowed me to enjoy my meal and take my time, which is exactly what I want when I'm out for a nice dinner. Overall, while the limit on some specialty items was a bit of a drawback, it was a minor complaint in what was otherwise an excellent dining experience. I would highly recommend Sushi Freak to anyone looking for high-quality, all-you-can-eat sushi in Las Vegas, and I look forward to going back and trying more of their unique dishes. With its great food, excellent service, and convenient hours, Sushi Freak is definitely a top choice for sushi lovers in the area.

The chicken fingers themselves were crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside, just the way I like them. The portion size was generous, and I appreciated the freshness of the ingredients. However, the experience was marred by the unpleasant interaction with the waitress. I understand that she might have been trying to maintain the secrecy of the sauce, but a simple description of its flavor profile would have sufficed. Instead, her curt response put a damper on my enthusiasm. Despite this, I can see why Raising Canes has a loyal following - the food is undeniably tasty. If the service had been more welcoming, I would have gladly given it a higher rating. As it stands, I would still recommend Raising Canes to fellow chicken finger enthusiasts, but with the caveat to be prepared for potentially inconsistent service. Perhaps it was just an off day, but first impressions matter, and unfortunately, mine was tainted by the attitude of the staff.

The air conditioning in the room is also extremely loud and sounds like it's on its last leg. The beds are comfortable, but the pillows are flat and lack any real support. The bathroom is clean, but the water pressure is weak and the shower head is old and clogged. The overall atmosphere of the hotel is just depressing, with faded decor and a general sense of neglect. The staff seems overworked and understaffed, which only adds to the frustration. I've stayed in better motels, and at least they didn't charge me extra for Wi-Fi. The fact that this hotel is still operating is a mystery to me. Unless you're desperate, stay far, far away from this dump. Trust me, you won't be saving any money in the long run with all the extra fees they'll nickel and dime you for.

The atmosphere was lively and relaxed, making it easy to mingle with fellow concertgoers. Overall, I had a fantastic experience and would highly recommend this venue to anyone looking for a unique and enjoyable concert experience. The combination of outdoor and indoor spaces, along with the creative installations, made for a memorable night out. I left feeling impressed and already looking forward to my next visit, hoping to catch another great show in this incredible setting.

The service was slow and our server seemed overwhelmed. Overall, it was an average experience, but the free kids meal helped make up for the disappointing salad and slow service, making it somewhat worth the visit on a Tuesday.
Overall, a pleasant dining experience with friendly service and generous servings, worth visiting for those looking to try German cuisine in a lively atmosphere somehow.

Overall, we had a fantastic experience and would definitely return. Matt's exceptional service and the unique atmosphere made our evening memorable. Although the goblet could use a bit more alcohol, it was still a fun and quirky touch. With a few minor tweaks, this place has the potential to become our new favorite spot. We're already looking forward to our next visit and recommending it to friends.

in the area that actually care about their customers and serve authentic, flavorful dishes. The decline of this establishment is disappointing, considering its initial reputation. With so many alternatives available, it's hard to justify a visit to this restaurant. Unless significant changes are made, I would not recommend wasting your time or money on a subpar experience. Sadly, this once-promising spot has lost its charm and appeal, making it a shadow of its former self.

I am still fuming as I write this review, and I feel it's my duty to warn others about the atrocious experience I had at this so-called diner. The fact that they tried to nickel and dime us for something as trivial as gyro sauce is laughable, and the fact that they had the audacity to call the cops on us is just ridiculous. The owner's behavior was completely unprofessional, and it's clear that he is more interested in scamming his customers than providing good service.

The food itself was mediocre at best, and the fact that we didn't even get to finish it because of the argument with the owner is just a waste. I demand to know how a business can stay afloat with such horrible customer service and blatant disregard for their customers' satisfaction. The fact that they are trying to sue me for the unpaid portion of the meal is just the cherry on top of this disastrous experience.

I would not recommend this place to my worst enemy, and I hope that anyone who reads this review will take my warning seriously. Save your money, save your sanity, and avoid this dump at all costs. The fact that they are trying to strong-arm their customers into paying for overpriced and subpar food is just a sign of desperation, and I have no doubt that they will be out of business soon. Mark my words, this place will be closed within a year, and it can't come soon enough. To anyone who is considering visiting this diner, let my experience be a warning to you: stay far, far away.

Overall, our experience at the buffet was enjoyable, with a wide variety of dishes to choose from and a few standout options, such as the chicken and waffles. The transition from breakfast to lunch was seamless, and we appreciated the omelette station and abundance of bacon. The service from the carver, David, and the bussers was top-notch, as they were attentive and ensured our table was always clear. However, our waiter, Jeff, could have been more attentive, especially when it came to refilling our drinks.

It's worth noting that some of the negative reviews we read before visiting seemed unfounded. For example, the complaint about the "rotten egg creme brulee" was likely due to the reviewer's mistake in trying the green tea creme brulee instead of the traditional creme brulee. We were pleased to see that the buffet had a clear sign indicating the different options.

One thing that did surprise us was the lack of certain high-end options, such as lobster or steak knives. While we didn't expect these to be included in the buffet price, it seemed like an odd omission for a establishment of this caliber. Despite this, we would still recommend the buffet to others, especially if they can take advantage of the Buffet of Buffet pass. However, we're not sure if we would be willing to pay the full price of over $60 per person, especially when there are other dining options available in the area.

Unfortunately, the lengthy wait overshadowed the taste and quality of my gyro calzone. The ingredients were fresh, and the flavors were well-balanced, but the delay made it difficult to fully appreciate. I understand that mistakes can happen, but consistent communication and accurate timing are crucial for a positive dining experience. Despite the food being good, the poor service and wait time led to an overall disappointing visit. With improved timing and communication, I would consider returning to Pickles to give them another chance to showcase their culinary skills. Perhaps a second visit will yield a better experience.

I was really looking forward to a delicious and satisfying bowl of pho, but what I got was a lackluster experience that left me disappointed and still hungry. The long wait for the food was frustrating, and the fact that our drinks were neglected for so long was just careless. When the food finally arrived, I was expecting a rich and savory broth, but instead, it was bland and uninspiring. The portion size was also smaller than what I'm used to, which didn't help to make up for the lack of flavor. Overall, my experience at this restaurant was a letdown, and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone, especially vegetarians who are already limited by the menu options. If you're craving good pho, do yourself a favor and head to the other restaurant up the street - trust me, you won't be disappointed.
The staff is friendly, and the atmosphere is lively, making it a great spot to catch a game or meet with friends for a delicious meal and drinks.

Overall, our experience at Fulton was decent, but not impressive. The fish and chips were average, and the chowder lacked flavor. Given the prices, I expected more generous portions and better taste. If I were to return, I'd definitely opt for the NY-style pizza, which seems to be a more popular and satisfying choice among customers. Perhaps Fulton shines more in their pizza offerings than their seafood options.

The atmosphere is lively and fun, making it perfect for a night out with friends. Overall, I highly recommend this spot for its delicious food, excellent drinks, and great service, all at a reasonable price, which keeps me coming back for more.

I was a bit apprehensive about the parking fee at first, but as I mentioned, the rate I got made it a non-issue. Plus, the peace and quiet of this place far outweighed the extra cost. The fact that it's a non-gaming, non-smoking property was a huge draw for me. I could finally enjoy a relaxing vacation without the hustle and bustle of the casinos. The staff were incredibly friendly and helpful, always willing to lend a hand or offer recommendations. The room was immaculately clean and well-maintained, with plenty of amenities to make our stay comfortable. We even took advantage of the fitness center and enjoyed the beautiful views of the strip while working out. The location is perfect - close enough to the action, but far enough away to escape the chaos. I've already booked my next stay here and I'm counting down the days until I can return. If you're looking for a tranquil oasis in the midst of the vibrant Las Vegas scene, look no further. Just be prepared to be spoiled - once you experience the luxury and serenity of this place, you'll never want to stay anywhere else on the strip again!

Overall, the food was delicious, but the high prices and minor service issues detracted from our experience. Despite this, the cozy atmosphere and tasty dishes might bring us back, albeit with a closer eye on the budget. With some adjustments to pricing and waitstaff etiquette, this comfort food spot could truly shine and earn a higher rating from us.

The overall experience was disappointing and frustrating. Poor communication and a lack of attentiveness from the waitress made our visit unpleasant. For a place I've visited before, this was a letdown. I expect better service, especially when it comes to handling mistakes and customer concerns. Unfortunately, the bad service overshadowed the food quality, making it unlikely for us to return anytime soon.

For that price, I expected a seamless experience. Instead, it was chaos and disorganization. The venue's lack of preparation and poor communication made for a frustrating night, leaving a sour taste despite the amazing performers and production quality of the event itself, which was the only redeeming factor.

I am extremely disappointed with the level of service I have received from Carmax, particularly given the fact that I purchased an extended warranty to protect myself from unexpected repairs. The repeated failure to diagnose and fix the issue with my front wheels has not only been frustrating, but it has also left me without a reliable vehicle on multiple occasions. The explanations I have been given for the problem have been unconvincing and have not addressed the root cause of the issue.

Furthermore, the paint oxidation issue on the roof and trunk lid is a concern that I believe should be covered under the warranty. However, I am hesitant to pursue this matter further with Carmax due to my past experiences with their service center. It seems that their primary goal is to get the vehicle in and out of the shop as quickly as possible, rather than taking the time to thoroughly diagnose and repair the problem.

I would advise anyone considering purchasing a vehicle from Carmax to think carefully before buying an extended service plan. While it may seem like a good idea at the time, the reality is that it may not provide the level of protection and service that you expect. In my experience, the plan has been more of a hindrance than a help, leaving me to deal with the frustration and inconvenience of repeated visits to the service center. Overall, I am extremely dissatisfied with my experience with Carmax and would not recommend their service plan to anyone.

I was disappointed but tried to remain understanding, considering the baristas seemed overwhelmed. However, as a customer, it's frustrating to experience such a significant delay, especially when others who ordered after me received their drinks promptly. The lack of organization and inefficient system is not the fault of the employees, but rather a management issue that needs to be addressed. With a few adjustments to their workflow and perhaps additional training, this location could provide the level of service that Starbucks is known for. Until then, I'll think twice before visiting this particular store, especially during peak hours.

The combination of flavors and textures is absolute perfection. I highly recommend trying their signature burger, it's a game changer. Although the seating area is limited, the food is easily enjoyed on-the-go. Don't be deterred by the long lines, the wait is well worth it. Friendly staff and quick service make the experience even more enjoyable. Overall, a must-visit for burger lovers in the heart of the city, near Times Square.

The ambiance was cozy and inviting, with traditional Indian decor that added to the overall experience. The prices were very reasonable, especially considering the high quality of the food and service. I was impressed by the attention to detail, from the flavorful dishes to the thoughtful touches like the scented hot cloths. The staff were knowledgeable and happy to make recommendations, which was helpful in navigating the extensive menu. Overall, I would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for authentic and delicious Indian cuisine in Madison. It's definitely a gem that I will return to on future visits.

I was a bit nervous trying a new style, but Rob's expertise and communication put me at ease. He took the time to explain each step of the process and made sure I was comfortable with the direction he was taking. The end result was a fantastic cut that exceeded my expectations. I've received numerous compliments and feel like a new person. The prices were also very reasonable, especially considering the high level of service I received. I'll definitely be back to see Rob for my future hair needs and would highly recommend him to anyone looking for a skilled and attentive stylist.

I had a bitter sweet experience with Freddy. He was able to come in almost immediately. And he installed the hot water heater. Although since he operates solo, you might have to help him with some heavy lifting. In my 30's that was not a problem but if you can't lift weights you might want to think twice or ask him to bring a helper.

Originally we agreed on a price of 575 dollars(for everything). However, because he said he will have to pay transaction cost of 3% for credit cards, I upped the total to 600(400 dollars on card) bucks. We also agreed that I will pay him 200 dollars in advance(once he starts the job).

After he was done I asked him to install 4 hand spray's. He proposed 40 bucks but then settled for 30 dollars. His power reciprocating saw gave up during the job so he had to cut through the existing copper pipes manually. Even still, he finished the job in about 70 minutes. Even at 120 bucks, this is a fair price. Considering, he was already there on the job and did not have to make an additional trip. But he decided to charge me at 35 a pop instead for a total of 140.

Gave him the card and he ran the car for 49.25 dollars more than we agreed. I asked him for a receipt but he told me since it was a manually keyed in amount he couldn't print one up.

I do have his handwritten invoice on me. On the invoice he did have 30 bucks originally which he struck out and made 35 for the hand spray. For the rest he put 35 dollars. For the heater he put 600 and put 200 dollars in advance. Even if you go by his numbers he was supposed to charge me 540 dollars on the card(Although we had agreed on 520 bucks) but instead he charged me 569.25.

I called him and he said he it must be the credit card machine that tacked on processing charges and he will send me a check for the extra cost. Its been more than 3 weeks but I still have to see a check in the mail. He has not responded to my messages to him either.

Bottomline:

He is available on short notice. He did a reasonable job(although he did say you do not need a drip pan under the heater. No No No. Don't take his advice on it. A drip pan is an insurance against hot water heater leaks which could result in thousands of bucks of savings if you ever have a leak).

However, do NOT trust him with your credit card. You are better off paying with cash. In my case it resulted in an ~50 dollars additional charge. It is still possible that he is planning on sending me a check but has not gotten around to it yet. If I see the check from him I will up my rating to 4 stars.

4 stars for service.
1 star for honesty.

Continuing from where I left off, I must emphasize the importance of being cautious when dealing with Freddy, especially when it comes to payment methods. While he may be reliable in terms of service and availability, his handling of credit card transactions leaves much to be desired. The fact that he charged me an extra $49.25 without providing a proper receipt or explanation is a significant red flag.

As I reflect on my experience, I am reminded of the importance of clearly communicating expectations and agreements when working with a service provider. In this case, I thought I had been clear about the payment terms, but somehow, there was a miscommunication that resulted in the extra charge. I hope that by sharing my experience, others will be more vigilant when dealing with Freddy or similar service providers.

In terms of the actual work done, I must say that Freddy was efficient and completed the installation of the hot water heater and hand sprays in a relatively short amount of time. However, his advice on not needing a drip pan under the heater is a concern, as it highlights a lack of attention to important safety and maintenance details.

Overall, my experience with Freddy has been a mixed bag. While he may be a reliable option for those in need of immediate service, his questionable business practices and lack of transparency when it comes to payment methods are significant drawbacks. As such, I would advise others to exercise caution when dealing with him and to carefully review any agreements or estimates before committing to his services.

In conclusion, I hope that Freddy will take my feedback to heart and work on improving his business practices, particularly when it comes to payment methods and communication. Until then, I would recommend that others approach his services with caution and carefully consider their options before committing to his work. With some improvements in these areas, I believe that Freddy could become a more trustworthy and reliable service provider, but for now, I can only give him 2 stars overall, with 4 stars for service and 1 star for honesty.

The lack of attention to detail and organization is staggering. It's clear that the staff is overwhelmed and unable to cope with the demands of a busy evening. The fact that they were out of clean wine glasses and took so long to deliver even the simplest of items is unacceptable. For a establishment that charges premium prices, you expect a certain level of service and quality, which they consistently failed to deliver. Unfortunately, my family and I will be taking our business elsewhere, seeking a more reliable and enjoyable dining experience.

Overall, a disappointing experience that left a bad taste, both literally and figuratively, due to the poor treatment and inattentive staff, making it unlikely for me to return or recommend to others anytime soon.

I've tried several options, and each one is a delicious twist. The staff is friendly, and the atmosphere is lively. Whether you're a local or just visiting, this hidden gem is a must-try for a quick, affordable, and satisfying meal that won't break the bank, making it an excellent choice.

I was shocked by the lack of attention and assistance from the salesperson. As a loyal customer, I expect a higher level of service, especially from a reputable brand like Nordstrom. The salesperson's abrupt behavior was unprofessional and made me feel unvalued. I ended up trying on the shoe myself and leaving without making a purchase. Unfortunately, this experience reinforced my decision to avoid the Chandler store and continue shopping at the Scottsdale location, where I consistently receive exceptional service and a wider selection of products. Nordstrom, please take note and address these issues.

As I reflect on my experience, I think it's essential to weigh the pros and cons before deciding to visit this day club. On one hand, the energetic atmosphere and top-notch stereo system make for an unforgettable experience, especially when a renowned DJ like Nicky Romero is performing. The crowd is lively and fun, and it's easy to meet new people, which is a significant plus. I also appreciate the fact that you don't need to have a table to find a seat, unlike in nightclubs, where this can be a significant drawback.

On the other hand, the overcrowding, particularly in the pool area, can be overwhelming. The constant splashing and beach balls being thrown around can make it challenging to relax and enjoy the surroundings. Additionally, the slow service at the bar is a significant concern, especially when you're paying a premium for drinks and water. The fact that you have to pay for water, which is essential in such hot weather, seems unfair and excessive.

The costs associated with visiting this day club are also a significant factor to consider. While getting in for free as a guest list member was a perk, the admission fees for guys can be steep, ranging from $70 to $80. The prices for umbrella and daybed rentals are also exorbitant, with a whopping $400 for a table. Drinks and food are similarly pricey, with tall plastic cups costing $15 each and sandwiches priced at $10. The $40 locker fee is also a significant added expense.

Despite these drawbacks, I believe that this day club is worth visiting if you're a fan of a particular DJ or looking for a unique experience. However, if you're on a budget or prefer a more relaxed atmosphere, you might want to consider alternative options. It's also worth noting that the hype surrounding this club might die down over time, which could make for a more enjoyable experience in the future.

In conclusion, my experience at this day club was a mixed bag. While I had an amazing time and enjoyed the music and atmosphere, the overcrowding, slow service, and high costs were significant drawbacks. If you're planning to visit, I recommend getting there early to take advantage of the free drink tickets, being prepared for the crowds and heat, and budgeting accordingly for the expenses. With the right mindset and expectations, you can still have a great time and enjoy the unique experience that this day club has to offer.

The combination of flavors and textures was perfect, making it a refreshing treat on a hot day. I appreciated the attention to detail, from the cup design to the fun gummy topping, which added to the overall enjoyable experience.

Overall, Big Grove offers a refreshing atmosphere and excellent service. The modern decor and open layout make it an ideal spot for casual gatherings or dates. Although the food didn't exceed expectations, the creative drink menu and attentive staff, like our outstanding waitress, make it worth revisiting. I look forward to returning and hopefully encountering the same exceptional service that made our experience memorable.

The lack of professionalism and disrespect towards patients is appalling. It's clear that the staff at the Thunderbird location are not being held to any standards, and it's reflected in the poor service they provide. As a patient, it's frustrating to be treated like an inconvenience rather than a person in need of medical care. The fact that they have the proper equipment is not enough to make up for the incompetence of the staff. I would not recommend Simon Medical to anyone, especially the Thunderbird location. Valley Radiology, on the other hand, has consistently provided me with a better experience, and I will be taking my business there from now on. It's time for Simon Medical to re-evaluate their staff and prioritize patient care.

The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, with friendly staff making it a perfect spot to unwind. We're already looking forward to our next visit to try more of their menu offerings and enjoy another round of their expertly crafted cocktails. Paymon's has won us over as happy hour regulars.

Overall, my experience at the cafe was exceptional, and I appreciated the attention to detail that the staff exhibited. It's clear that the team takes pride in their work, from the thorough cleaning of silverware to the prompt service. Tsvetelin, my waiter, was particularly impressive, ensuring that my take-out order was ready quickly and accurately. The food itself was also outstanding, with the Irish Steel Cut Oatmeal being a highlight. The portion sizes were generous, and the prices were very reasonable, especially considering the high-quality ingredients and preparation. As someone who often prefers a more personalized dining experience, I appreciated the alternative to a buffet that this cafe provided. The views from the huge glass windows were an added bonus, making for a lovely atmosphere. I would definitely return to this cafe and highly recommend it to others, whether they're looking for a quick bite or a leisurely meal. The combination of excellent service, delicious food, and comfortable surroundings makes it an ideal choice for anyone staying in the hotel or visiting the area.

Overall, the experience was disappointing, especially considering the prices. The atmosphere was lively, but that wasn't enough to make up for the subpar food and slow service. Our server seemed overwhelmed, and it took a long time to get the check. The food, although tasty at the start with the appetizers, fell short with the main courses. With so many other great dining options available, I wouldn't recommend this place unless they seriously step up their game. For now, I'll be taking my business (and my appetite) elsewhere.

Overall, the experience was marred by the subpar service, which is unfortunate given the promising food and ambiance. Despite the delicious options and generous spread, the poor treatment by the staff left a sour taste. It's a shame, as the restaurant has potential, but until they address their customer service issues, I wouldn't recommend it to others. For a establishment that charges premium prices, one would expect a higher level of service. Perhaps with some additional training for their staff, they can improve and live up to their full potential, but for now, I can only give them three stars.
Overall, a pleasant dining experience with friendly service and flavorful food, despite a few minor missteps, making it a decent choice for those seeking a casual meal in a cozy atmosphere.

The frustration and disappointment were palpable. Basic amenities were also lacking, and the overall cleanliness was subpar. The hotel's inability to resolve issues promptly and politely made the experience even more unbearable. Needless to say, I will never recommend this hotel to anyone and advise others to explore alternative accommodations to avoid similar ordeals.

Overall, the convenience of having a Post Office inside is overshadowed by the outdated cash-only policy. It's frustrating to be forced to use the nearby ATM and incur an additional fee. Despite this, the store's vast party supply selection remains a draw. However, the Post Office's restrictive payment methods leave a sour taste, making my overall experience at Bubbles of Joy somewhat disappointing.

Overall, the experience was mixed, with timely service and quality work, but poor communication and unexpected costs left a negative impression, making us hesitant to recommend or reuse their services in the future.

"Extremely disappointed with the overall experience and lack of effort to rectify issues. For the prices, I expected much better quality and service. Needless to say, I won't be returning and would recommend others to explore alternative options for a more authentic and satisfying dining experience."

The lack of cleanliness and unappetizing food preparation was staggering. As a parent, it's disturbing to see such disregard for customer health. The pizza itself was bland and overpriced. Needless to say, our experience was thoroughly disappointing. The combination of poor service, unhygienic practices, and subpar food ensures that we will never return to this establishment. It's clear that the owner's absence was not the only problem that Sunday afternoon.

Overall, our experience at this gourmet burger joint was decent, but not impressive enough to warrant a return visit. The prices were a bit steep for the quality and portion sizes we received. The service was friendly and attentive, but the food didn't quite live up to our expectations. The unique offerings, such as the boozy shakes and creative burger toppings, were a nice touch, but the execution fell short. Perhaps with a few tweaks to their menu and portion sizes, this place could reach its full potential. As it stands, we appreciated the convenience of being able to walk here from the Cosmopolitan, but we wouldn't go out of our way to recommend it to others. With so many other great dining options in the area, this place just didn't stand out from the crowd.

Overall, the service was disappointing and unfriendly. The waitress's attitude and lack of apology were unprofessional. For a restaurant with nice ambience, the poor service and overpriced food were major letdowns. I would not recommend l'Avenue to anyone, especially those who like a little heat in their meals. The experience was subpar and left a bad taste, literally and figuratively, making it unlikely for me to return or suggest it to others.

For the long flight to and from Philly, I've taken US Airways twice now. Neither time was I impressed.

Was it the cheapest option: yes. And that's how 90% of us purchase tickets, so I doubt the things we complain about will really improve.

Somehow on US Air, the seats feel even narrower than the competition despite the fact they fly the same 737s and A319s in the same configuration. But, I had no problem with finding overhead space, which is rare nowadays, so that earns them a bump.

No seatback TVs is a downer on a cross-country flights, no TVs of any kind was a bit surprising (though a relief: if I can't control it, I hate having something running in the background).

They ran out of food before reaching all the way in the back (though prices were better than the airport to be fair). But the attendants were helpful, professional, and did a second round of drinks.

Will I fly them again? Probably, but if there's a flight on United or better for an extra $30 I'd probably take that. Overall, my experience with US Airways was mediocre at best. While they excelled in terms of friendly staff and affordable prices, the lack of amenities and cramped seating left much to be desired. As a budget-conscious traveler, I appreciate the cost savings, but I also value comfort and entertainment during long flights. Unless US Airways makes significant improvements to their in-flight experience, I'll likely opt for other airlines in the future, even if it means paying a bit more.

The hostess, who claimed to be the manager, showed no interest in listening to our concerns or apologizing for the poor service we experienced. Instead, she seemed put off by our feedback and didn't even attempt to offer a solution or compensation for the inconvenience. As we left, I couldn't help but feel disappointed and frustrated by the whole experience. The lack of attention to detail, from the broken table to the uncomfortable chairs, was evident, and the staff's attitude only made things worse. It's clear that this establishment is not prioritizing customer satisfaction, and it's unfortunate because the location and ambiance had potential. However, with such horrible service, I would not recommend this place to anyone. The fact that the hostess/manager was so unapologetic and unprofessional is a major red flag, and it's likely that others have had similar experiences. Needless to say, we will never be returning, and I hope that in the future, the management will take customer feedback seriously and make a genuine effort to improve their service. Until then, I would advise others to steer clear of this establishment and take their business elsewhere.

Despite the chaos, the atmosphere of the restaurant itself was pleasant and the outdoor seating area was well-maintained. The food, although not entirely accurate, was flavorful and satisfying. The fajita chimmichonga was a nice surprise, and we enjoyed it nonetheless. Our server's efforts to keep up with the demanding tables were appreciated, and we felt sorry that he had to deal with the rowdy party. Overall, the experience was not ideal, but the quality of the food and the potential for a more peaceful evening on a different night would bring us back to give it another try.

but perhaps for dessert or brunch. The atmosphere was cozy and inviting, with a unique decor that added to its charm. Our server was attentive and knowledgeable, making great recommendations. Despite the food being just average, the presentation was appealing and the portions were generous. Overall, it was an decent experience, but not impressive enough to warrant a return visit for a full meal. With a few tweaks to their menu and seasoning, this restaurant could reach its full potential and become a top choice in the area. For now, it's a maybe.

The service wasn't much better, with our server seeming overwhelmed and inattentive. It took ages to get the check and even longer to pay. The atmosphere was lively, but that's about where it ended. For a place that's supposed to be a popular brunch spot, I was thoroughly unimpressed. The prices were also steep considering the subpar quality of the food. Overall, my experience was a major letdown, and I would not recommend this place to anyone. There are far better options out there, and I'll be taking my business (and my dessert cravings) elsewhere.

To make matters worse, the food itself was a letdown. The crepes were overcooked and lacked any real flavor, which was a shock given the high prices they were charging. The fillings were sparse and didn't seem fresh, which further added to our disappointment. We left feeling frustrated, hungry, and ripped off. The whole experience was a disaster from start to finish, and it's clear that the management and staff are not taking customer satisfaction seriously.

The contrast between this place and Cafe Monte in South Park couldn't be more stark. Not only are the crepes at Cafe Monte made with love and care, but the atmosphere is warm and inviting, and the service is top-notch. The staff are friendly and attentive, and the managers clearly care about their customers' experiences. It's clear that Cafe Monte is a labor of love, whereas this place seems to be just a money-making venture with no regard for quality or customer satisfaction. If you're looking for a great crepe experience, do yourself a favor and avoid this place at all costs. Go to Cafe Monte instead, and taste the difference for yourself.
Very disappointing experience, slow service, and limited drink options made for an unpleasant dining atmosphere overall at this establishment unfortunately.

As I sat there, trying to enjoy my meal despite the uncomfortable seating and our waiter's unpleasant demeanor, I couldn't help but think about the pizza itself. The round pizza, which my companion ordered, was a different story altogether. The crust was perfectly cooked, with just the right amount of crunch and chew. The sauce was tangy and rich, and the mozzarella was creamy and well-balanced. It was a classic New York-style pizza, and it did not disappoint.

But, as I mentioned earlier, the Sicilian pizza was a letdown. It was greasy and overwhelmed by the tomatoes, which made it difficult to eat. I found myself using a knife and fork, which, as a native New Yorker, felt like a sacrilege. The flavors were good, but they were overpowered by the grease and the excessive tomato sauce. And, at $17 for half a pie, it felt like a pricey mistake.

Despite the mixed bag of food, I was impressed by the little touches that the restaurant had to offer. The water bottles that sat on the table were a nice touch, and the heavy plates made in France added a touch of elegance to the meal. The modern pizza tower, which displayed the pies in a sleek and stylish way, was also a nice touch. However, it was somewhat lost on me, given my sunken-down seat and uncomfortable position.

As we finished our meal and prepared to leave, I couldn't help but think about the impromptu firepit lawn party that had introduced me to Dom DeMarco's pizza in the first place. The cold Sicilian slice that I had eaten that night had been a revelation, and I had been eager to try more. While our experience at the restaurant was not without its flaws, I was glad that I had gotten to try the pizza in a more formal setting.

In the end, I decided to give Dom DeMarco's four stars, despite the uncomfortable seating and our waiter's unpleasant demeanor. The food was good, if not great, and the little touches that the restaurant had to offer were appreciated. But, as I always say, "You CAN eat the atmosphere," and the ambiance of the restaurant was a major factor in my decision. If they can work on their seating and service, I have no doubt that Dom DeMarco's will become a top destination for pizza lovers in Las Vegas.

As we left the restaurant and walked out into the cool night air, I couldn't help but feel a sense of nostalgia for the old neighborhood pizzerias of Brooklyn. There's something about a classic New York-style pizza that just can't be beat, and Dom DeMarco's had come close to capturing that magic. While it wasn't perfect, I was glad that I had gotten to experience it, and I would definitely be back for more. With a little tweaking, I have no doubt that Dom DeMarco's will become a favorite among locals and visitors alike.

As I reflect on my 3-day stay, I'm still trying to process how a hotel with such great amenities and some exceptional staff members could fall so short in terms of overall service. The pool, as I mentioned, was truly a highlight - it was beautifully maintained and provided a wonderful oasis from the hustle and bustle of the city. The valet team, led by John, were always courteous and friendly, and the shuttle service was convenient and reliable. Patty, the phone operator, was a shining star - always answering my calls with a smile and addressing me by name. These individuals truly embodied the spirit of hospitality, and I appreciate the effort they put into making my stay more enjoyable.

However, the front desk and room service staff were a different story altogether. The snobbish attitude and unhelpful demeanor of the check-in agent set the tone for a disappointing stay, and the rudeness of the room service staff was simply unacceptable. When I ordered room service, I was greeted with a dismissive tone and a lack of options - it seemed like everything I wanted was unavailable. As someone who has worked in the hospitality industry, I was shocked by the lack of courtesy and professionalism.

But the final straw was when I approached the front desk about the issues with my room. The fact that the window didn't open and the room was causing me significant discomfort and allergic reactions was concerning, to say the least. I expected some kind of apology or offer of assistance, but instead, I was met with a shrug and a suggestion that maybe I was just having an allergic reaction or that the previous guests had sneaked in a cat. The lack of empathy or concern was staggering, and the fact that they couldn't even offer me some basic amenities like cream or Benadryl was appalling.

As I said, I didn't want to give this hotel a 1-star review, but the cumulative effect of these negative experiences left me no choice. I had convinced my family to stay here, and I felt like I had let them down. Despite the great pool, wonderful valet and shuttle staff, and excellent housekeeping, the poor service and lack of concern from the front desk and room service staff overshadowed everything. I hope that the hotel will take my feedback seriously and take steps to address these issues, because with a little bit of effort, this could be a truly great hotel. Until then, I would caution others to think carefully before booking a stay here.

As I reflected on our experience, I couldn't help but feel that the chaos of the environment contributed to the mistake with our bill. It's understandable that a popular spot like this would be busy on a Saturday morning, but the frenetic pace seemed to prioritize turnover over accuracy and customer satisfaction. The food, while tasty, didn't particularly stand out as exceptional or memorable, which made the inflated price tag even more disappointing. 

I would caution future visitors to double-check their bills carefully before paying, as the staff's haste to process orders and clear tables can lead to errors. In our case, the mistake was significant, and the added tip only compounded the issue. Despite the pleasant company of our friends, the overall experience was marred by the crowded and noisy atmosphere, as well as the billing mishap. 

If you do decide to visit, be prepared for a lively and fast-paced environment, but also be vigilant about your order and bill. It's a shame, really, as the place has potential, but the emphasis on speed and efficiency seems to come at the expense of attention to detail and customer care. Perhaps a return visit at a less busy time would yield a more positive experience, but for now, I would approach with caution and a keen eye on the bill.

The overall experience was disappointing, to say the least. Not only was I overcharged for my meal, but the staff's attitude towards the mistake was unprofessional and dismissive. It's not acceptable for a business to display incorrect pricing and then blame it on an "old price" without taking any responsibility or apologizing for the inconvenience. The fact that Irany and her coworker laughed it off and didn't even offer a discount or a gesture of goodwill was insulting. As for the food, while the chicken was flavorful, the lack of effort in preparing the rest of the burrito was evident. For a burrito that's supposed to be a signature item, it was surprisingly lacking in flavor and texture. Needless to say, I won't be recommending this place to anyone, and I'll be taking my business elsewhere. The combination of poor customer service and subpar food is a recipe for disaster, and I'm not willing to give them another chance.

The rare steak was cooked to perfection and the portions were generous. Although the service can be slow, the food quality makes up for it. Overall, it's a great spot for a late-night bite in Vegas, and I'll definitely be back for another delicious #11. The flavors and value keep me coming back.

The food, although tasty, was overpriced for the portion size and the wait time. It's understandable that a waterfront location comes with a premium, but the value just wasn't there. The atmosphere, however, was lively and entertaining, with a mix of locals and tourists. The people-watching, as I mentioned, was top-notch, and the scenery was indeed beautiful. With a few tweaks, such as allowing pets on the deck and streamlining their service, this place could really thrive. As it stands, it's an average spot with potential. Perhaps with some adjustments, they can attract a more consistent crowd and live up to their full potential. Until then, it's a decent spot to grab a bite and enjoy the view, but don't expect to be blown away.

Overall, our experience was disappointing, especially considering the high ratings. The lobster gnocchi, a highly-recommended dish, was overcooked and lacked flavor. The fact that one of my friends fell ill after eating the chicken raises concerns about food safety. While I'm willing to give them the benefit of the doubt, our visit was a letdown, and I wouldn't rush to return anytime soon, hoping it was indeed just an off night.

The quality of the meats was impressive, with each cut cooked to perfection. The Churrasco Sirloin "Picanha" Style was a standout, with a beautiful char on the outside and a tender, juicy interior. The Huli Huli Chicken Hawaiian Style was also a favorite, with a sweet and smoky flavor that complemented the richness of the other meats. The service was attentive and efficient, with the staff continually offering refills on drinks and clearing plates. Overall, it was a fantastic dining experience, and I would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a high-quality Brazilian steakhouse experience. Just be prepared for a lot of food and a lively atmosphere.

The presentation was beautiful and the cookies were packaged nicely. The girls loved the unique flavors and we all enjoyed the sweet treats. I would definitely recommend this company for any special occasion, especially for those looking for something a little different. Their customer service and attention to detail made the experience even more special and memorable.

Unfortunately, the bad service outweighs the good coffee. I've visited multiple times, hoping for improvement, but the attitude remains the same. Until they address this issue, I'll take my business elsewhere, despite the unique atmosphere and delicious drinks. Perhaps with some customer service training, this place could reach its full potential and become a truly enjoyable spot to relax and unwind with a great cup of coffee.

The Wicked Spoon buffet truly exceeded my expectations in every way. The variety and quality of the dishes were exceptional, and the presentation was impressive. I was particularly impressed by the made-to-order stations, where chefs were preparing dishes fresh on the spot. The service was also top-notch, with friendly and attentive staff constantly refilling drinks and clearing plates. The atmosphere was lively and modern, with a sleek and sophisticated decor that added to the overall upscale feel of the buffet. One thing to note is that the buffet can get quite crowded, especially on weekends and during peak hours. However, the efficient layout and multiple serving lines helped to minimize wait times and ensure a smooth experience. Overall, I would highly recommend the Wicked Spoon buffet to anyone looking for a high-end dining experience in Las Vegas. Be sure to come hungry, as you'll want to try a little bit of everything. With its incredible selection, excellent service, and modern atmosphere, the Wicked Spoon buffet is a must-visit destination for foodies and buffet enthusiasts alike. Whether you're celebrating a special occasion or just looking for a unique dining experience, the Wicked Spoon is sure to impress.

In addition to the attractive wait staff, the overall atmosphere of Crown & Anchor is cozy and inviting, making it an ideal spot to catch up with friends or watch a game. The pub's decor is traditional, with dark wood accents and vintage British memorabilia adorning the walls. The crowd is lively, but not too rowdy, and the staff is attentive and knowledgeable about the drinks menu. Speaking of which, the selection of beers is impressive, with a range of options to suit every taste, from crisp lagers to rich, malty ales. The whiskey collection is also noteworthy, with a variety of premium labels to choose from. While the presence of video poker machines is still a drawback, Crown & Anchor does its best to minimize their impact on the overall ambiance. Overall, if you're looking for a classic pub experience in Vegas, Crown & Anchor is a solid choice. Just be prepared for a few distractions from the video poker machines, and you'll be all set for a fun and memorable night out. With its winning combination of good drinks, tasty food, and lively atmosphere, Crown & Anchor is a must-visit destination for anyone seeking a authentic pub experience in the heart of Vegas.
Staff are knowledgeable and friendly, making shopping a pleasant experience every time, with excellent product advice.

Unfortunately, the rest of our experience at Cibo was just as underwhelming. The salads we ordered were lackluster, with wilted lettuce and bland dressings. It seemed like they were phoning it in with their ingredients, relying on the trendy atmosphere to carry the meal. Our server was friendly, but seemed overwhelmed and inattentive at times, taking a while to refill drinks and clear plates. For a restaurant that prides itself on its Italian cuisine, the execution was shockingly poor. As someone who values a good pizza above all else, I was disappointed to find that Cibo's pies fell so far short of expectations. The combination of tough crust, sparse toppings, and unremarkable flavors made for a meal that was forgettable at best. Unless they seriously revamp their menu and cooking techniques, I wouldn't recommend Cibo to anyone looking for a satisfying Italian meal. The quaint ambiance and extensive drink menu are not enough to redeem the subpar food. Unless they make some significant changes, I'll be taking my pizza cravings (and my appetite) elsewhere. Overall, a disappointing experience that left a bad taste in my mouth.

The talent and dedication of the performers were evident in every aspect of the show, from the flawless vocals to the meticulous costume designs. I was particularly impressed by the attention to detail in the costumes, wigs, and makeup, which truly transformed the male performers into their female counterparts. I must say, my initial disappointment with the Golden Nugget's renovations has given way to a mix of emotions after seeing the website's promises of a revamped pool area. While I was looking forward to experiencing the hotel's amenities during my stay, the reality was far from it. The constant construction and "coming soon" signs made it feel like I was staying in a hotel that was still under development. However, the idea of trained dolphins and tiki hut cabanas spun from gold is undeniably exciting, and I can see why someone would want to come back and experience it.

Despite the hotel's shortcomings during my visit, there were some highlights that made my stay somewhat enjoyable. The real estate conference, for instance, was well-organized and informative, and I appreciated the opportunity to learn from industry experts. The 13.99 champagne buffet brunch, although not exactly gourmet, was a fun experience, and the mimosas were a nice touch. And, of course, the in-room movie selection was a great way to pass the time, with some truly obscure films that I wouldn't have seen otherwise.

But I must reiterate, the true star of the show was the world-famous bread pudding. I'm not even kidding when I say it's a must-try. It's a game-changer. If you're planning to visit the Golden Nugget, do yourself a favor and save room for dessert. With the promised renovations and additions, I'm willing to give the hotel another chance in the future. Maybe by June, when everything is supposed to be completed, the Golden Nugget will live up to its full potential. Until then, I'll just have to keep dreaming about that bread pudding and the prospect of lounging by the new pool, surrounded by trained dolphins and golden tiki huts.

I must say, the transformation in my Bloodhounds, Gunner and Gabby, is nothing short of miraculous. Before working with Nate, I was at my wit's end, feeling like I'd tried every possible solution to address their behavioral issues. But from the very first session with Nate, I knew I'd found someone special. His approach is not just about training the dogs, but also about educating the owners on how to effectively communicate with and manage their pets.

One of the things that impressed me most about Nate is his patience and understanding. He took the time to explain everything in a way that made sense to me, and he never made me feel like I was doing anything wrong. He simply showed me a better way, and that made all the difference. The fact that he was willing to take Gunner in for a month to work with him one-on-one is a testament to his dedication and commitment to his craft.

The results speak for themselves. Gunner's aggression is gone, and he's now a joy to be around. Both dogs are well-behaved, and they listen to commands without hesitation. We can take them on walks without being dragged down the street, and they'll even do a two-hour down-stay without any issues. It's amazing to see how far they've come, and I owe it all to Nate and his expertise.

I've already recommended Nate to several friends and family members, and I'll continue to do so. His training methods are kind, gentle, and effective, and he's always available to answer questions or provide guidance whenever I need it. The group training sessions on Saturdays are also a great bonus, as they provide an opportunity for my dogs to socialize with other dogs and for me to continue learning and refining my skills.

In addition to his training services, Nate's boarding facilities are top-notch. I recently had to go out of town for a week, and I was able to board my dogs with Nate without any worries. I knew they'd be well taken care of, and they'd even get to enjoy their daily walks and training sessions. It's a huge relief to know that my dogs are in good hands when I'm away.

In conclusion, I want to express my heartfelt gratitude to Nate for all that he's done for my family and me. He's not just a dog trainer; he's a miracle worker. If you're struggling with your dog's behavior or just want to improve your relationship with your pet, I highly recommend giving Nate a try. You won't regret it. With Innate Dog Training, you can expect proven results, a supportive community, and a trainer who truly cares about you and your dog. Thank you, Nate, for everything!

As I reflected on my experience at Great Wall, I couldn't help but compare it to my usual haunt, Golden Buddha. The dim sum at Golden Buddha is always freshly prepared and presented with a variety of options, even during off-peak hours. In contrast, the limited selection and lackluster quality of the dishes at Great Wall left me underwhelmed. The atmosphere, although bustling during peak hours, felt tired and worn by the time we arrived, with the two carts struggling to keep up with the demand.

Despite my disappointment, I do want to acknowledge that the staff were friendly and apologetic, recognizing that they were running low on options. However, the overall experience was marred by the subpar food and chaotic service. For a dim sum enthusiast like myself, the thrill of the experience lies in the discovery of new flavors and the excitement of flagging down carts laden with steaming hot delicacies. Unfortunately, Great Wall failed to deliver on this front, and I found myself missing the comfort and reliability of Golden Buddha. Unless I hear that they've revamped their dim sum service, I'll be sticking to my trusted favorite. Perhaps I'll give Great Wall another chance during peak hours, but for now, I'm content to return to the familiar and satisfying experience of Golden Buddha.

The lunch buffet, while abundant in options, lacked the authenticity and flavor I've come to expect from a Thai restaurant. Each dish tasted like a watered-down version of its traditional counterpart, with the Tom Yum soup being a major letdown - it was lukewarm and devoid of the spicy kick that typically characterizes this beloved Thai dish. The Pad Thai was unrecognizable, and the orange chicken was cloyingly sweet, overpowering any other flavor that might have been present. Given the extremely affordable price point of $6.99, I can see why this place might appeal to those prioritizing quantity over quality. However, for someone who values authentic, expertly prepared Thai cuisine, this establishment falls short. As such, I wouldn't return, opting instead to drive a bit further to Spring Mountain for a genuinely satisfying Thai dining experience at Thai Style Noodle House.

If I were to come back, I'd probably try something else on the menu, like the pho or banh mi, to see if they do those dishes better. Overall, it was an average experience, but I can see why people in the area might like it as a convenient option for Vietnamese cuisine.

Overall, I would not recommend this hotel to anyone and will be taking my business elsewhere. The lack of attention to detail and cleanliness is a major red flag, and I would advise others to think twice before booking a stay here.

As I reflected on my experience at Pizzeria Bianco, I couldn't help but think that the hype surrounding this institution is not only justified but also necessary. It's a place that has captured the hearts and taste buds of pizza enthusiasts, chefs, and celebrities alike, and for good reason. The combination of Chris Bianco's passion for traditional Neapolitan-style pizza, the cozy and intimate atmosphere, and the exceptional quality of the ingredients all come together to create a truly unforgettable experience.

One of the things that struck me most about Pizzeria Bianco was the attention to detail that goes into every aspect of the restaurant. From the carefully curated selection of wines and craft beers to the eclectic decor of the waiting area, it's clear that every element has been thoughtfully considered to create a unique and immersive experience for guests. And then, of course, there's the pizza itself – perfectly cooked, flavorful, and expertly balanced, with each bite a masterclass in texture and taste.

I've had my fair share of pizza in my lifetime, but Pizzeria Bianco's offerings are in a league of their own. The white pizza, with its delicate balance of creamy mozzarella, fragrant garlic, and fresh arugula, was a revelation – a testament to the power of simplicity and restraint in cooking. The margherita, with its classic combination of San Marzano tomatoes, mozzarella, and basil, was equally impressive, with each ingredient shining in perfect harmony. And the "mainly meat" pizza, with its rich prosciutto and savory mushrooms, was a hearty and satisfying delight.

What's perhaps most remarkable about Pizzeria Bianco, however, is the way it has managed to maintain its integrity and commitment to quality despite the overwhelming demand and attention it has received. In an era where restaurants are often tempted to compromise on ingredients, portion sizes, or cooking techniques in order to keep up with the crowds, Pizzeria Bianco remains steadfast in its dedication to traditional methods and exceptional ingredients. It's a testament to the power of passion and perseverance, and a reminder that, with hard work and attention to detail, even the smallest and most humble of restaurants can achieve greatness.

In short, Pizzeria Bianco is a must-visit destination for anyone who loves pizza, cooking, or simply great food. It's a place that will leave you inspired, delighted, and perhaps even a little changed – a culinary pilgrimage that will stay with you long after you've finished your meal and left the restaurant. So, as I said earlier, get on the next flight to AZ, or hop in your car and drive down the 101. Trust me, the wait will be worth it.

Whether you're celebrating a special occasion or just looking for a relaxing getaway, the Bellagio is sure to impress. We highly recommend it to anyone looking for a high-end hotel experience.

As I paddled along the Allegheny River, I couldn't help but feel a sense of awe at the stunning views of the Pittsburgh skyline. The sun was shining, casting a warm glow over the city, and the occasional cloud provided a welcome respite from the heat. I had chosen to head down towards the point, and as I paddled alongside the submarine by the Science Center, I felt like I was in a different world. The surreal experience of being next to such an impressive vessel was exhilarating, and I couldn't help but take a moment to appreciate the unique perspective on the city that kayaking provided.

As I continued on my journey, I noticed the variety of wildlife that calls the river home. I spotted a few fish swimming in the water, and even caught a glimpse of a bird or two soaring overhead. The peacefulness of the river was a welcome change from the hustle and bustle of city life, and I found myself feeling relaxed and at ease as I paddled along. The sound of the water lapping against the kayak and the occasional cry of a seagull were the only sounds I needed to feel completely at peace.

One of the things that I appreciate most about Kayak Pittsburgh is the convenience and accessibility of their location. As I mentioned earlier, it's just a short walk from PNC Park, and the staff is always friendly and helpful. They provide everything you need to get started, from the kayak and paddle to the life vest and safety instructions. They even offer tips and advice for navigating the river, which is especially helpful for beginners.

As I paddled back upriver, I couldn't help but think about how much I loved this city. Pittsburgh has a way of surprising you, whether it's the stunning views from the top of Mount Washington or the vibrant cultural scene in the Strip District. And kayaking on the river is just one more way to experience all that the city has to offer. Whether you're a native Pittsburgher or just visiting, I highly recommend adding Kayak Pittsburgh to your list of things to do. It's an experience you won't soon forget, and one that will leave you feeling refreshed, renewed, and ready to take on whatever the city has in store.

In addition to the scenic views and relaxing atmosphere, kayaking on the river also provides a great workout. Paddling against the current can be challenging, but it's a great way to build strength and endurance. And the sense of accomplishment you feel when you finally make it back to the dock is unbeatable. Whether you're looking for a fun and relaxing activity or a challenging workout, kayaking on the river has something to offer.

As I finished up my kayaking trip and returned to the dock, I couldn't help but feel grateful for the experience. Kayak Pittsburgh had provided me with a unique and memorable experience, and I couldn't wait to get back out on the water again. With its convenient location, friendly staff, and stunning views, Kayak Pittsburgh is a must-visit destination for anyone looking to experience the best of Pittsburgh. So why not get out there and start paddling? I promise you won't regret it!

As I sat on the monorail, feeling queasy and disappointed, I couldn't help but think that our experience at Battista's was a major letdown. The food, although my wife enjoyed her dish, was subpar and overpriced. The atmosphere, while quaint and nostalgic, couldn't make up for the lackluster cuisine. I've been to plenty of Italian restaurants in my day, and Battista's just didn't cut it. The fettucine alfredo was a disappointment, and the fact that I started feeling sick after eating it was a major red flag. I'm not sure if it was the food itself or something else, but it was definitely a turning point in our evening.

We had been having such a great time in Vegas, exploring the city and trying new restaurants. Ellis Island and the Gold Coast buffet were highlights of our trip, and we were excited to try more local eateries. But Battista's was a misstep, and I would caution others against wasting their time and money.

In retrospect, I wish we had taken the reviews more seriously and avoided Battista's altogether. The warnings about the accordion player and the overpriced food were spot on, and we should have listened. Instead, we ended up with a disappointing and expensive meal that ruined our evening.

If you're looking for good Italian food in Vegas, keep looking. There are plenty of other options that are sure to satisfy your cravings without breaking the bank. And if you're a fan of Bally's, like we are, there are plenty of other great restaurants and attractions to explore in the area.

In conclusion, our experience at Battista's was a major disappointment, and I would not recommend it to anyone. With so many other great options available in Vegas, it's just not worth the risk. Stick with the tried and true favorites, like Ellis Island and the Gold Coast buffet, and avoid this overpriced and underwhelming Italian restaurant.
The service was also appalling, with rude staff and long wait times, making the overall experience utterly unbearable and regrettable, leaving a lasting bad impression.

Overall, the experience was disappointing. The food was lacking and overpriced. I left still hungry and unsatisfied, unlikely to return or recommend this place to others due to the poor service and subpar cuisine.
