With some improvements in these areas, Pewter Rose could once again become a top choice for brunch in the city. For now, I would caution others to manage their expectations and hope that the restaurant can get back on track soon.

As I reflect on my overall experience, I'm left with mixed emotions. On one hand, I adore the unique theme, decor, and uniforms - it's clear that Rick Moonen's team has put a lot of thought into creating an immersive atmosphere. The inventive drink menu is also a highlight, with some truly standout options. And, of course, the mac and cheese is an absolute must-try - it's creamy, crunchy, and utterly delicious.

On the other hand, the food is a bit of a mixed bag. While the chick pot pie nuggets and fried oxtail show promise, they ultimately fall short due to flavor imbalances. The French Onion Dip Sandwich is a particular disappointment, lacking the richness and depth that I've come to expect from a dish like this. It's clear that the kitchen is still experimenting and refining their recipes, which is understandable given that the restaurant is still in its early days.

The service, too, is a work in progress. While the hostesses are friendly and stylish, our server seemed a bit disorganized and inattentive. The fact that our appetizers arrived before our drinks not once, but twice, is a bit baffling. However, the "apprentice" who assisted with water service was a bright spot, providing excellent recommendations and a warm, friendly demeanor.

The surprise visit from Rick Moonen himself was a lovely touch, and it's clear that he's committed to making a personal connection with his customers. As the restaurant continues to find its footing, I'm hopeful that this level of attention and care will become more consistent throughout the dining experience.

For now, I'd recommend RM Seafood downstairs for a more polished and refined dining experience. However, if you're in the area and looking for a fun, casual spot to grab appetizers or drinks, this new restaurant might be worth a try. Just be aware that they're still working out the kinks, and be sure to order that mac and cheese - it's a game-changer.

In six months or so, I'd love to return and see how the restaurant has evolved. With a bit more time to refine their menu and service, I have no doubt that this place will become a top destination in Mandalay Shoppes. Until then, I'll be keeping an eye on their progress and looking forward to my next visit. For now, I'd give this restaurant 3.5 stars - a solid effort, but not quite a home run just yet.

The prices are relatively affordable, making it a decent option for those on a tight budget. However, the trade-off is the lack of high-quality products and limited brand selection. Despite this, I've managed to find some hidden gems and decent deals on occasion. If you're looking for a one-stop shop with a wide range of budget-friendly sporting goods, this store might be worth a visit, but don't expect to be blown away by the shopping experience.
The staff is knowledgeable, and their attention to detail is impressive, making every visit a pleasant experience.

The atmosphere is cozy, with a trendy vibe that feels somewhat forced. Prices are reasonable, but the need to pay immediately after ordering can be off-putting. Overall, The Sparrow is a decent spot for a casual drink, but it lacks a genuine, laid-back ambiance, making it just an average experience. Worth a visit for the drinks, but don't expect to be blown away by the overall experience or exceptional service.

Overall, the experience was decent, but the pricing strategy seems a bit off. The quality of the food is a step above traditional fast food, but the prices don't quite reflect the convenience factor. That being said, the pizza was a highlight, with a crispy crust and flavorful toppings. The garlic bread was also a nice touch, served freshly baked and aromatic. However, the runny Alfredo sauce was a disappointment. With a few tweaks to the pricing and sauce consistency, this place could be a real winner, offering a unique blend of quality and convenience in the Italian fast-casual scene.

The food was mediocre and lacked creativity, with small portions that didn't justify the high prices. Overall, I was disappointed and would not recommend Red Velvet to anyone looking for a quality vegan or vegetarian experience in Vegas. With so many other excellent options available, it's easy to find better value and service elsewhere. Unless they revamp their menu and service, I won't be returning.

As I walked out, I couldn't help but think that the gym had missed an opportunity to gain a new member. The facility itself seemed well-equipped and clean, and the fact that there were no wait times for equipment was a major plus. However, the lack of attention to customer service and the inconvenience of not being able to discuss membership options at a time that suited me was a significant turn-off. I understand that mistakes can happen, and it's possible that the staff was simply having a bad day. Nevertheless, as a potential customer, I expect a certain level of service and flexibility, especially when it comes to something as important as signing up for a membership.

I'm still interested in joining the gym, but the experience has left a sour taste in my mouth. I'll have to make a concerted effort to return during their designated hours, which may take some time given my unpredictable work schedule. It's a shame, really, because I think the gym has a lot to offer, and I would have liked to have been able to give them a full 5-star review. As it stands, the 3-star rating reflects my disappointment with the customer experience, but I'm willing to give them another chance to show me that they can do better. Hopefully, next time I visit, I'll be able to have a more positive interaction and get the information I need to make an informed decision about joining.

The service was friendly and attentive, adding to the overall pleasant experience. I appreciated the generous portion sizes and affordable prices. The atmosphere, although simple, was clean and inviting. Overall, I'm glad I stumbled upon this hidden gem and would definitely recommend it to others looking for a delicious and unique dining experience in the area.

Overall, we left feeling satisfied and already planning our next visit. The prices were reasonable, and the portions were just right. We're excited to try more of their menu items, especially the daily specials. The chef's creativity and attention to detail truly shine through in each dish. We highly recommend this hidden gem to anyone looking for authentic, mouth-watering cuisine in a cozy setting.

We've always had friendly service at Osha Thai, and last night was no exception. The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, making it a great spot for a casual dinner with friends. While the food may not have blown us away, it was still enjoyable and satisfying. The ability to bring our own wine definitely adds to the experience, and the small corking fee is a fair trade-off. Overall, Osha Thai is a solid choice for Thai food in the area, and we would recommend it to others. Just be aware that the portions may be smaller than expected, and don't forget to try the excellent Chai Tea.

Despite the potential for delicious dumplings, my experience at Qing Hua was marred by questionable business practices and inconsistent food preparation. The fact that some dumplings are served from frozen while others are made fresh to order raises concerns about quality control and transparency. Furthermore, the cash-only policy and shady receipt handling practices are major red flags. As a customer, I expect honesty and integrity from the businesses I support. Unfortunately, Qing Hua's actions have led me to lose trust in their establishment. With better options available, such as Restaurant Mai Xiang Yuan, I see no reason to return to Qing Hua and risk being taken advantage of again. The higher prices and dubious practices are not worth the potential taste, making it an easy decision to take my business elsewhere.

Overall, not impressed and wouldn't recommend. For the price, expected much better quality and taste. Maybe they were just having a bad day, but our experience was disappointing. Will not be returning, even with coupons, as there are better options available for a similar price range elsewhere.

Overall, I'd recommend it for special occasions. The upscale atmosphere and stunning views make it perfect for impressing a date or celebrating a milestone. Despite the high prices, the exceptional service and elegant setting make it well worth the splurge, leaving a lasting impression on all who visit.
and see if their other menu items live up to the tasty breakfast I had, maybe their sandwiches or salads will impress me just as much as the pancakes did initially.

Overall, it's the perfect spot to relax and unwind. The menu offers a variety of delicious options, and the staff are always friendly and attentive. Whether you're looking for a quiet spot to work or a cozy atmosphere to catch up with friends, this restaurant has something for everyone. With its charming ambiance and excellent amenities, it's no wonder it's my top choice in town.

As we finished our meal and prepared to leave, I couldn't help but feel underwhelmed by the overall experience. The rushed service and lack of attention to detail from the hostess stand set the tone for a meal that, while had some highlights, ultimately fell short of expectations. The food, as I mentioned, was a mixed bag - the antipasta appetizer and pasta with vodka sauce were truly exceptional, but the meatballs and fussilli with spicy sausage were just okay. The fact that the meatballs were served lukewarm was a disappointment, and the overcooked sausage was a shame.

Despite the knowledgeable and accommodating waiter, the overall service felt frenetic and disjointed. The constant requests to clear our plates, even when they were still full, made us feel like we were being pushed out the door. And the strange habit of sitting on chairs that blocked access to our booth was just plain awkward. It's not what I expect from a high-end restaurant like Rao's, especially given the steep prices.

As we left the restaurant at 7:00, I was struck by how empty it was. Given the strict reservation policy and the fact that we were told 5:00 was the only available time slot, I expected the place to be bustling. Instead, it felt like we were being herded in and out to make way for...no one. It was a strange and unsettling feeling, and it only added to my overall sense of disappointment.

In the end, I would caution others to approach Rao's with tempered expectations. While the food can be excellent, the service and overall experience are in need of serious attention. Until they can iron out these issues and provide a more cohesive and welcoming experience, I would hesitate to recommend it to others. And as for me, I'm not sure I would be willing to give the Harlem version a try, despite my initial curiosity. Sorry, Rao's - you've got some work to do.

Overall, my experiences at this spot have been pleasant, and I appreciate the laid-back atmosphere. The staff is friendly, and the service is prompt, even when it gets busy. I've been here with friends and family, and everyone has enjoyed themselves. The pool tables are a great addition, and the patio area is perfect for warmer nights. While it may not be the fanciest place, it has a certain charm that keeps me coming back. I've even started to appreciate the quirky crowd that filters in later at night, although I still make it a point to head out before things get too rowdy. For a casual night out with friends or a low-key spot to watch a game, I would definitely recommend giving this place a try. Just don't expect fancy cocktails or gourmet food – it's a no-frills, laid-back bar that delivers on its promises.

Despite the minor setbacks, I was impressed by the sheer variety of options available at India Palace. The Chicken Tikka was cooked to perfection, and the Naan bread was soft and fluffy. The Veggie Korma was also a highlight, with a rich and creamy sauce that complemented the vegetables nicely. I was a bit disappointed with the Dosas, which were slightly greasy, but overall, the food was satisfying and filling. The desserts, particularly the Gulab Jamun, were a nice touch and provided a sweet ending to the meal. While India Palace may not be the best Indian restaurant I've been to, it's definitely a great value for the price. With a bit of refinement in their service and attention to detail in their food preparation, India Palace could easily become a top contender for Indian cuisine in the area. For now, I'm willing to give them another chance and see if they can improve on their minor flaws. Overall, I would recommend India Palace to anyone looking for a affordable and decent Indian meal on the Strip.

The level of disrespect and racism we experienced was appalling. It's unacceptable to prioritize certain customers over others based on their appearance or ethnicity. The fact that we were removed from our seats to accommodate a group of suited men is a clear indication of the establishment's biases. The waitress's behavior and the management's decision left a sour taste, overshadowing the initially delicious food. We will not recommend this place to anyone, and our Valentine's Day celebration was thoroughly ruined. The $300 spent was not worth the humiliation and degradation we faced.

The atmosphere was cozy and welcoming, with a rustic decor that added to the overall barbecue joint experience. Our server was attentive and knowledgeable, happy to answer our questions about the menu and make recommendations. The prices were very reasonable, especially considering the generous portion sizes. We left feeling full and satisfied, already planning our next visit. The fact that they make their desserts in-house is a big plus, and we're excited to try more of their offerings in the future. Overall, we're glad we gave this location a try and can see why it's the original - it's clear that they're doing something right. We'll be back soon to sample more of their delicious barbecue and homemade treats. This location has definitely won us over, and we recommend it to anyone looking for a great barbecue experience.

The atmosphere was modern and trendy, with a vibrant bar area that added to the overall ambiance. Our server was attentive and knowledgeable, helping us navigate the menu and making excellent recommendations. Prices were reasonable, especially during happy hour, making it a great spot for a night out with friends or a casual date. Overall, I was impressed and would definitely return to try more of their creative dishes and enjoy their lively atmosphere again.

The return process itself was relatively painless, but the lack of customer service skills from the staff was noticeable. They seemed overwhelmed and understaffed, which added to the overall frustration of the experience. As I waited in line, I took a glance around the store and was disappointed to see that many of the products they once carried were no longer available. The store seemed to be prioritizing quantity over quality, with rows of cheaply made items that didn't appeal to me. The narrow aisles and disorganized shelves made it difficult to navigate, and I found myself eager to leave as soon as my return was processed. Overall, my experience at Bed Bath and Beyond was underwhelming, and I left feeling like the store had lost its touch. I'm not sure if I'll be back anytime soon.

J'ai été agréablement surpris par la qualité du service et la rapidité de la préparation des plats. Le personnel était sympathique et attentionné, ce qui a contribué à rendre mon expérience encore plus agréable. La propreté des locaux était également impeccable, ce qui est important pour moi lorsqu'il s'agit de choisir un endroit où manger. En résumé, le Club Sandwich est un excellent choix pour ceux qui cherchent un endroit où se restaurer après une soirée de fête ou simplement pour satisfaire une envie de nourriture rapide et délicieuse. Je recommande vivement cet établissement et j'y retournerai certainement pour essayer d'autres plats de leur menu.

The salad was fresh but unremarkable, and the flatbread, while tasty, didn't justify the upscale prices. Overall, the experience felt like paying for ambiance rather than cuisine. The Market Square theory holds true - the scenery is lovely, but the food is overpriced and underwhelming. Perhaps that's the trade-off for dining in a prime location, but I won't be returning for the food alone.

The atmosphere was cozy and intimate, with dim lighting and comfortable seating, making it an ideal spot for a romantic evening out. The service was also top-notch, with friendly and attentive staff who were happy to answer questions about the menu and make recommendations. I was impressed by the creativity and presentation of each dish, and the portion sizes were generous without being overwhelming. The prices, as I mentioned, were very reasonable, especially considering the high quality of the food and the generous serving sizes. Overall, I would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a delicious and memorable dining experience without breaking the bank. The combination of excellent food, cozy atmosphere, and friendly service makes it a standout in the area, and I'm already looking forward to my next visit. Whether you're a foodie or just looking for a great night out, this restaurant is definitely worth a try.

The experience was thoroughly disappointing, and it's clear that the server was not interested in providing good customer service. The fact that we had to ask multiple times for simple things like straws and refills on our drinks was frustrating, and the delay in receiving our garlic bread was unacceptable. The food itself was average, nothing special, and the portion of extra meat sauce was laughable. But what really sealed the deal for me was the server's attitude when I asked about sherbet for my kids. A simple "yes" or "no" would have been sufficient, but instead, I was met with a huff and a shoved menu. It was clear that the server was not interested in accommodating our needs or providing good service.

As a parent, it's frustrating to have to deal with this kind of attitude, especially when you're trying to enjoy a meal with your family. The fact that they got two stars from me is solely due to their large portion sizes, but that's not enough to make up for the poor service and average food. I won't be returning to this restaurant, and I would not recommend it to others. There are plenty of other restaurants in the area that provide better food and better service, and I will be taking my business (and my family) elsewhere. Overall, it was a disappointing experience, and I hope that the restaurant will take steps to improve their service and accommodate the needs of their customers.

Overall, my experience was disappointing, considering the high prices they charge. The atmosphere was nice, with the aquatic displays, but the service and flexibility with menu options fell short. For a restaurant that specializes in seafood, I expected more freshness and flavor in their dishes. Unfortunately, the subpar food and rude waiter made my lunch break unpleasant, and I wouldn't recommend this place to colleagues or friends looking for a quality dining experience.

I am still fuming when I think about the experience I had at Tireworks. The fact that they tried to take advantage of me, a female customer, is absolutely appalling. I'm glad that I had the presence of mind to seek a second opinion, which ultimately saved me over $2,000. It's unacceptable that a reputable business would engage in such deceitful practices.

The contrast between the initial diagnosis and the actual repair needed is staggering. Tireworks claimed that my car required a multitude of expensive repairs, including new rotors, brake pads, hoses, calipers, and a master cylinder. Meanwhile, Master Transmission Automotive, a trustworthy and honest shop, determined that all I needed was a simple brake fluid flush.

I want to emphasize that this is not just a case of a mistaken diagnosis; it's a deliberate attempt to exploit a customer's lack of knowledge and vulnerability. As a woman, I've often been warned about the potential for mechanics to take advantage of me, and unfortunately, Tireworks proved those warnings to be true.

In conclusion, I would strongly advise against taking your vehicle to Tireworks. Not only did they try to rip me off, but they also demonstrated a blatant disregard for honesty and integrity. If you value your hard-earned money and want to ensure that your car is properly serviced, take it to a reputable shop like Master Transmission Automotive. They will treat you with respect, provide an accurate diagnosis, and charge you a fair price for the necessary repairs. Avoid Tireworks at all costs, and beware of their predatory practices.

The hotel's amenities, although limited, were well-maintained and sufficient for a budget-friendly stay. The casino on site was a nice touch, offering a convenient spot to grab a drink or try my luck. While the clientele may have been a bit rough around the edges, the staff were friendly and accommodating. Overall, I'd recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a no-frills, affordable option near the strip. It's not the fanciest place, but it gets the job done and won't break the bank. For the price, it's a solid choice.

I gave it one star because its only saving grace is that the kitchen is open late...and it serves Pepsi.

I ordered (so typical of me) their supersomethinggooey chimichanga. You may as well have brought me a pile of flaming poo. It looked so unappetizing when it was plunked down in front of me. You know when you were a kid and you were forced to eat something you hated and you did all you could to prolong the agony? Well, there were no potted plants within range for me to dump my food in and the napkins were so flimsy I couldn't spit my bites out gracefully. Instead, I pushed away the food and claimed, "I savored every bite and now I'm full. I'll take it home." My friend loves that place. Why? I couldn't understand it, either. I dumped the leftovers off in the trash at the Taco Bell I ended up at.

Service was crap, food was crap, parking was crap. It's located around the corner from my husband's old office...but hell, if the die-hard alkies of my husband's office wouldn't go there, that's saying something. Geez, it's stumbling or in their case, tumbling, distance from work. Even happy hour couldn't persuade the guys to go. Yes, it's that bad. You know it's bad when the alcoholics say no.

Thank god it's all you can drink Pepsi or I wouldn't know what to do with myself. *rolls eyes* I know what I'd do - I'd go to Jack in the Box across the street and bring it over because JITB is better than whatever Dos Gringos could ever try to feed me.

PS -- What's up with those park benches for tables? It seems like they raided a city park and brought the furniture back to the restaurant. The overall atmosphere was chaotic and uninviting, with loud music and dim lighting that made it difficult to see the subpar food they were serving. To top it all off, the restrooms were filthy and had a strange odor that lingered throughout the restaurant. Needless to say, I will not be returning to Dos Gringos anytime soon. In fact, I would advise others to steer clear of this establishment and opt for one of the many other, far superior dining options in the area. With so many better choices available, it's hard to imagine why anyone would voluntarily subject themselves to the disappointment and disgust that is Dos Gringos.

The constant changes in departure time were not only frustrating but also made it difficult for us to plan our time effectively. We were left feeling trapped and helpless, stuck on a plane with no clear idea of when we would finally take off. The lack of communication and inconsistent updates from the airline staff only added to our frustration. As a loyal customer, I expect more from Southwest, especially when it comes to providing accurate and reliable information. The affordable tickets and free bags are great perks, but they don't make up for the poor service and mismanagement we experienced. I hope Southwest takes steps to improve their communication and customer service to prevent similar experiences in the future.
Disappointing experience overall, would not recommend to anyone due to poor quality and unfriendly staff.

The atmosphere and energy of the place were infectious, making it easy to overlook the subpar drinks. I'd definitely recommend it to friends, but advise them to pace themselves or drink elsewhere. Despite the pricey drinks, I'm already looking forward to my next visit and dancing the night away with great company.

The lack of effort to resolve my issue is appalling. It's clear that customer satisfaction is not a priority. With numerous other dining options available, it's disappointing to see a business neglect its patrons so blatantly. I strongly advise others to explore alternative restaurants that value their customers and provide decent service, rather than wasting time and money at this subpar establishment.

The lack of attention to customers and disorganization was really frustrating. It's a shame, because the atmosphere of the place has potential, but the service and management seem to be lacking. The "Wall" challenge experience was the final straw for me, as it showed a complete disregard for customer loyalty and retention. Having to start over from scratch every day because they couldn't keep track of my card was infuriating. I had been willing to give them the benefit of the doubt, but after multiple disappointments, I decided it was time to take my business elsewhere. Overall, I would not recommend this place to anyone looking for a reliable and customer-focused dining experience.

The lack of attention to detail and organization at the LAS airport check-in counter set the tone for a somewhat underwhelming experience with Virgin. As we boarded the flight, we were expecting a more luxurious atmosphere, but unfortunately, it felt like a typical economy flight. The seats were cramped, and the legroom was barely sufficient. The fact that they charged $2 for earphones and didn't offer any complimentary snacks was a bit disappointing, especially considering the $25 luggage fee. The in-flight entertainment was limited, and the selection of movies and TV shows was not impressive. The flight attendants were friendly, but the overall service felt rushed and impersonal. When we arrived at SFO, the mistake with the baggage claim only added to our frustration. Overall, our experience with Virgin at LAS was subpar, and we would likely consider other airlines for our future travels. The extra fees and lack of amenities made it feel like we were not getting a good value for our money.
The combination is unique and flavorful, making it a must-try for burger lovers, with great service to top it off perfectly every time.

Overall, the unassuming exterior belies a gem of a breakfast spot. Friendly service and generous portions add to the charm, making Omelet House a must-visit for anyone seeking a satisfying morning meal in Las Vegas. Despite the mediocre coffee, the exceptional food and warm atmosphere ensure a pleasant dining experience that will keep you coming back for more.

Overall, our experience was underwhelming. The service was friendly, but the food didn't live up to our expectations. For a place with a decent reputation, we were disappointed by the lackluster flavors and dry textures. Perhaps they were just having an off day, but based on our visit, I'd recommend exploring other options in the area, like Wolfgang or Social House, for a more satisfying lunch experience.

I was thoroughly embarrassed by the whole experience and couldn't wait to get out of there. The food, when it finally arrived, was just average and didn't make up for the poor service. I've heard mixed reviews about At HoT since then, but my experience was so subpar that I haven't felt inclined to give them another chance. It's a shame, really, because the atmosphere is nice and the location is convenient. However, with so many other great restaurants in the area, I just don't see myself returning to At HoT anytime soon. Unless they seriously revamp their service, I'd advise others to think twice before stopping in.
"Service was friendly and attentive, prices reasonable, making it a great spot for a casual breakfast or brunch with family and friends, definitely worth a visit for their delicious baked goods."

Overall, despite the less-than-stellar service, I would still recommend this restaurant for its delicious cuisine and generous servings. The atmosphere was also cozy and inviting, making it a great spot to relax and enjoy a meal. Although our server seemed a bit inattentive, the quality of the food made up for the shortcomings in service. With its convenient location and reasonable prices, this restaurant is a great option for those looking for a satisfying dining experience. I would definitely consider returning on my next visit.

I'm still fuming as I write this review, thinking about the atrocious service we received at Shibuya. The fact that the waiter couldn't even be bothered to check on us regularly or offer any kind of decent service is appalling. And when I brought my concerns to the manager, I expected some kind of apology or attempt to rectify the situation, but instead, he seemed completely uninterested and unhelpful.

The whole experience was just a disaster from start to finish. We had to ask multiple times for refills on our drinks, and even then, it took an inordinate amount of time to get them. The food, as I mentioned, was irrelevant at that point, because the service was so bad that it completely overshadowed anything that might have been good about the meal. And to top it all off, the waiter had the nerve to embarrass me in front of my friends by telling me that my credit card was declined, when in reality, it was just a blatant lie.

I've dined at some of the top restaurants in Las Vegas, and I can confidently say that Shibuya is one of the worst. The fact that they have good reviews is baffling to me, and I can only assume that they must be fake or from people who have extremely low standards. If you're looking for a good dining experience in Vegas, I would strongly advise against going to Shibuya. There are far better options available, with staff who actually care about providing good service and ensuring that customers have a positive experience.

In fact, I would go so far as to say that Shibuya is a black mark on the Las Vegas dining scene, and it's a wonder that they've managed to stay in business this long. Unless they seriously overhaul their staff and service, I wouldn't recommend this place to my worst enemy. Save your money, save your time, and save your sanity - avoid Shibuya at all costs. One star is even too generous for this dump, and I'm only giving it that because the review platform won't let me give it zero stars.

As I reflect on our experiences, I'm reminded that the food was indeed the highlight of our visits. The menu offered a diverse range of options, and the dishes we tried were flavorful and well-presented. However, the inconsistencies in service and the issue with the Visa gift card left a sour taste in our mouths. It's a shame, really, because the location is perfect for us, and we were hoping to find a new go-to spot.

Despite the convenience and decent food, the lackluster service and the gift card debacle have deterred us from returning. It's not that we're expecting exceptional service every time, but a little friendliness and attention to detail can go a long way in making customers feel valued. The bartender we met on our first visit was a great example of this, but unfortunately, our servers on subsequent visits didn't quite live up to that standard.

In the end, I'd say that this place has potential, but it needs to work on providing more consistent and welcoming service to its customers. Until then, I'd recommend it to others with caution, suggesting that they manage their expectations and perhaps try it out during off-peak hours when the staff might be more attentive. For us, though, it's unlikely that we'll be back anytime soon, which is a pity, given its proximity to our home and the promise of its menu.

Overall, my experience at this hotel was a letdown, and I would not recommend it to others until the construction is completed and the issues with the rooms are addressed. The slow-draining tub was a major inconvenience, and the smell of urine in the walkway to the Strip was unbearable. While the room was clean and housekeeping was responsive, it wasn't enough to make up for the other problems. If you're looking for a budget-friendly option, you might want to consider other hotels in the area that don't have these issues. For me, the hassle and discomfort weren't worth the savings, and I'll be willing to pay more for a better experience in the future. Perhaps with some renovations and improvements, this hotel could reach its full potential, but for now, I'd advise others to look elsewhere.

I'm extremely disappointed in the level of service and attention to detail at the meat market. As a customer, it's frustrating to feel like you're being upsold on products you don't need, and then to have mistakes made with your order. The fact that I received a different cut of meat than what I paid for is unacceptable, and it's not something that I'm willing to overlook. The bakery, on the other hand, has shown some promise with their donuts, but the inconsistency in their inventory is a problem. If they're going to advertise that they have certain products, they should make sure to have them in stock.

It's a shame, really, because I had high hopes for this place. I love supporting local businesses, and I was excited to have a quality meat market and bakery in the area. But after my experiences, I just can't bring myself to go back. The lack of attention to detail and the pushy sales tactics have left a bad taste in my mouth. I've taken my business elsewhere, and I wouldn't recommend the meat market to anyone. The bakery might be worth a try if you're in the area and they have what you're looking for, but be prepared for the possibility that they might not have the products you want. Overall, I'm disappointed and frustrated with my experiences at this establishment, and I don't see myself returning anytime soon.

As we sat down to enjoy our lunch buffet, the attentive staff ensured that our glasses were always filled with refreshing drinks, such as mango lassi or chai. The service was prompt and courteous, with the staff happily answering our questions about the various dishes on offer. The buffet spread was constantly replenished, ensuring that the food was always fresh and hot. I was impressed by the variety of options available, catering to both vegetarians and non-vegetarians alike. The quality of the food was consistently high, with each dish expertly prepared and presented.

One of the standout features of Spice 9 is its ability to balance flavors and spices, creating a truly authentic Indian dining experience. The dishes were not overly rich or heavy, allowing the natural flavors of the ingredients to shine through. I was particularly impressed by the tandoori chicken, which was cooked to perfection and had a beautiful smoky flavor. The naan bread was also freshly baked and delicious, perfect for scooping up the various curries and sauces on offer.

Overall, I was thoroughly impressed by Spice 9 and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a delicious and authentic Indian meal. The combination of excellent food, attentive service, and upscale atmosphere makes it a great option for both casual lunches and special occasions. I'm already looking forward to my next visit, when I can try more of the dishes on the menu and explore the restaurant's full potential. With its convenient location and ample parking, Spice 9 is sure to become a favorite among locals and visitors alike.

The lack of hygiene and professionalism is appalling. I've witnessed numerous incidents of cross-contamination and neglect of basic food safety protocols. Needless to say, I will not be returning to this location and would advise others to avoid it due to the egregious health concerns and poor management.

Unbelievable experience, lack of trust with the staff. Obvious scam targeting unsuspecting patrons, leaving a sour taste. Management needs to address this issue promptly to regain customer confidence and prevent further incidents of blatant theft. Until then, beware and double-check your change carefully.

Overall, our experience at Hooters was extremely disappointing. The combination of smaller, overpriced wings and nickel-and-diming for condiments like ranch dressing left a bad taste in our mouths. The lack of transparency from our server, Ashlea, regarding the extra charges was also frustrating. It's clear that Hooters is more focused on making a quick profit than providing good value to their customers. With so many other restaurants offering similar food and atmosphere at better prices, it's hard to see why we would ever choose to go back to Hooters. As we said, we'll be sticking to Zipps from now on, where the food and service are consistently better.

As I continued to explore the hotel and its surroundings, I realized that the location was truly the gem of this property. Being in the mid-strip area, I had access to some of the best dining options, shows, and attractions that Vegas has to offer. I was able to walk to the Mirage and catch a performance of LOVE, the Beatles-inspired Cirque du Soleil show, which was absolutely breathtaking. The next night, I strolled over to the Venetian and enjoyed a delicious dinner at Wolfgang Puck's Posto, followed by a gondola ride through the canals.

The convenience of having so many great restaurants and shows within walking distance was a major perk, and I found myself taking advantage of it every night. I also appreciated the fact that I could easily grab a coffee or snack at one of the many cafes and eateries in the area, without having to venture too far from my hotel.

Another benefit of staying at this hotel was the monorail stop, which made it easy to get to other parts of the strip without having to deal with traffic. I took the monorail to the MGM Grand to see the Lion Habitat, and then headed to the Mandalay Bay to check out the Shark Reef Aquarium. The monorail was a convenient and affordable way to get around, and I appreciated having it as an option.

In terms of the hotel itself, I was pleasantly surprised by the quality of the rooms. As I mentioned earlier, they had been renovated and were more than adequate for my needs. The bed was comfortable, the bathroom was clean and well-appointed, and the TV had a good selection of channels. I also appreciated the fact that the hotel offered a range of amenities, including a fitness center, a pool, and a business center.

Of course, no review of a Vegas hotel would be complete without mentioning the casino. As I said earlier, the casino at this hotel is not the most exciting or impressive, but it does have its perks. The table games are affordable, and the dealers are friendly and knowledgeable. I was able to get a $5 craps table, which was a great way to spend an afternoon, and the Pai Gow tables were also reasonably priced.

One thing to note is that the parking at the hotel can be a bit of a challenge. The valet service can be slow, and the self-parking garage can be crowded and confusing to navigate. However, I always managed to find a spot, and the hotel staff were helpful and accommodating when I needed assistance.

Overall, I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a convenient and affordable place to stay in Vegas. The location is unbeatable, the rooms are comfortable and well-appointed, and the casino has its perks. While it may not be the most luxurious or exciting hotel on the strip, it is a great value for the price, and I would definitely stay here again.

In fact, I would go so far as to say that this hotel is a hidden gem on the strip. It may not have the glitz and glamour of some of the other hotels, but it has a certain charm and character that makes it stand out. The staff are friendly and welcoming, the rooms are clean and comfortable, and the location is unbeatable. Whether you're a first-time visitor to Vegas or a seasoned pro, this hotel is definitely worth considering.

So, if you're looking for a great place to stay in Vegas without breaking the bank, I would highly recommend this hotel. Don't be intimidated by the negative reviews or the fact that it's not one of the fancier hotels on the strip. This hotel has a lot to offer, and I think you'll be pleasantly surprised by its charms. Book a room, grab a drink at the bar, and get ready to experience all that Vegas has to offer. You won't regret it!
Very disappointed, won't be returning to this location due to poor service and limited new menu options available now sadly.

The staff is knowledgeable and friendly, making the browsing experience even more enjoyable. I appreciate the interactive displays and the overall modern aesthetic of the store. However, I still think they're missing out on some revolutionary products, like that iPlug implant. Until then, I'll just have to keep dreaming of a hands-free future and stick to visiting the store for its entertainment value.

Despite the occasional disruptions from inconsiderate patrons, the restaurant's warm atmosphere and exceptional value always draw me back. The staff's friendly demeanor and accommodating nature make up for any minor inconveniences. I appreciate the consistency in their food quality and the generous portions they provide. It's clear that the restaurant prioritizes customer satisfaction, and I've never had a bad experience with my orders. Overall, I highly recommend this establishment to anyone seeking a delicious meal at a reasonable price, and I will continue to be a loyal customer, tolerating the occasional unpleasantness from fellow diners.

that are far superior to this dump. The lack of amenities and poor customer service are just the tip of the iceberg. I've stayed in budget-friendly hotels that offered more comfort and convenience than this place. The fact that it's still under construction is no excuse for the subpar experience we're having. The front desk staff seems completely uninterested in helping guests, and the overall atmosphere is just uncomfortable. I'm extremely disappointed and would not recommend this hotel to my worst enemy. The fact that we got our room comped and still feel ripped off says a lot about the quality of this establishment. Save your money and your sanity, and book a room at a reputable hotel. Trust me, you won't regret it. This place needs a major overhaul before it's even worth considering. Until then, it's a hard pass from me.

Overall, our experience at this buffet was disappointing, and we left feeling that the Groupon deal was the only redeeming factor. The subpar food and unfriendly service made it clear that this establishment is not prioritizing its customers' satisfaction. The fact that the workers seemed uninterested in our needs and the food had been sitting out for a while was a major turnoff. While the roasted carrots and flan were a pleasant surprise, they were not enough to make up for the overall lackluster experience. The absence of cellphone signal and the expensive wifi option only added to our frustration. Considering the numerous other dining options available, it's unlikely that we will return to this buffet, even with another Groupon deal. Unless they make significant improvements to their food quality and customer service, we would not recommend this place to others.

Mammoth Transportation helped make our Vegas wedding extra special. We rented "Tiny" to transport our wedding group of about 25 people to the chapel, locations around the strip for photos and then to nightclubs for us to celebrate.

"Tiny" was definitely not tiny by any means; our group was very comfortable in the spacious limo. It was clean and had a great sound system. We were able to bring our own alcohol, and cups and ice were provided.

Our driver, Scott, did an excellent job. He was friendly, personable and professional. He went above and beyond what was required of him. He even helped hook us up with a deal for bottle service at one of the clubs.

I highly recommend using Mammoth. The overall experience was top-notch, and the price was very reasonable. Mammoth Transportation truly helped make our special day unforgettable, and we can't thank them enough for their exceptional service.

Considering the price of $7.99 for the Classic Gyro and Side Salad, I expected a more welcoming atmosphere. Unfortunately, the dark and run-down decor, combined with the boozy smell, made for an uninviting experience. The wobbly tables and late opening didn't help either. Despite the decent food, the overall ambiance and service issues would make me think twice about returning. Maybe they'll work on improving these aspects, but for now, it's an average rating from me. The gyro itself was flavorful, but the negatives outweighed the positives in this visit.

Despite the initial letdown, I was pleased to discover a diverse range of dining options, from casual eateries to upscale establishments. The location, situated along the river, offers beautiful views and a pleasant atmosphere. I can imagine it being a lovely spot to relax and enjoy a meal during warmer months. However, my visit lacked the vibrancy I had anticipated, which made it feel somewhat underwhelming. Perhaps, as my coworkers suggested, summer is the best time to experience Station Square in its full glory, with more events and activities drawing in larger crowds. I'm willing to give it another try then.

The atmosphere is warm and inviting, making it easy to browse and relax. Christina's passion for flowers is evident in every arrangement, and her customer service is top-notch. I left feeling uplifted and already planning my next visit. The unique flower selection and personalized service make Bud & Vine a standout. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a special gift or a beautiful pick-me-up.

The stark contrast between this disastrous dining experience and the pleasant visit to In-N-Out was astonishing. For a fraction of the cost, In-N-Out provided superior quality food and exceptional customer service. It's clear that this BLT establishment is resting on its name rather than striving to deliver a memorable experience. With subpar food and atrocious service, it's a wonder they remain in business. Unless they drastically revamp their operations, I would not recommend this place to anyone. The memory of that horrible meal still leaves a bad taste, and I'm grateful for the redemption found at In-N-Out.

I've been to this establishment multiple times and have never been disappointed. The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, making it perfect for dates or special occasions. The staff's attention to detail is impressive, and they genuinely seem to care about their customers' experiences. Overall, I highly recommend this place to anyone looking for a top-notch dining experience, and I will undoubtedly be returning to indulge in their exceptional cuisine again.

Overall, my experiences at this restaurant have been consistently underwhelming, despite the welcoming atmosphere and decent beverage selection. The food, unfortunately, falls short of expectations, with the cilantro lime dressing being a notable misstep. However, the variety of vegetarian and vegan options is a redeeming quality, making it a tolerable choice for dining with friends who follow those diets. The service, thankfully, has always been a highlight, with friendly and patient staff who handle the sometimes-rowdy crowd with professionalism. While I appreciate these positives, the subpar food quality prevents me from giving a higher rating, leaving me to wonder if this restaurant will ever live up to its potential.

Overall, a pleasant visit with some drawbacks. Prices were a bit steep, but the atmosphere and service made up for it. I'd recommend for a casual outing, just be aware of the smaller drink portions and higher prices, and plan accordingly to make the most of your experience.

The atmosphere is casual and welcoming, making it a great spot for families or groups of friends. The lanes are well-maintained, and the staff is friendly and helpful. They also have a small arcade area with a few games, as well as a snack bar that serves basic bowling alley fare like hot dogs, nachos, and sodas. The prices for food and drinks are reasonable, and they also offer specials and deals on certain days of the week. Overall, this hidden bowling alley is a great find, offering a fun and affordable bowling experience with plenty of opportunities to save money through their various specials and promotions.

Despite the desserts not quite living up to my lofty expectations, I must commend the presentation and creativity that goes into each and every one of them. The attention to detail is truly impressive, and it's clear that the pastry chefs take pride in their work. I was particularly fond of the unique flavor combinations, such as the rose tea macaron, which was a fascinating twist on traditional macaron flavors.

However, the prices do seem a bit steep for the portion sizes, and I couldn't help but feel that I was paying more for the ambiance and presentation than the actual taste and quality of the desserts. That being said, I do appreciate the experience and the opportunity to try such beautifully crafted treats.

The Bellagio location was bustling with activity, and it was clear that this was a popular destination for both locals and tourists alike. The Aria hotel location, on the other hand, was a bit more subdued, but still maintained a lively and elegant atmosphere. Overall, I would recommend this establishment to anyone with a sweet tooth and a appreciation for the finer things in life. While it may not have been a home run for me in terms of taste, the presentation and creativity were certainly noteworthy, and I would be willing to give them another try in the future.

As the night wore on and the wait for the checks continued, the atmosphere in the restaurant began to shift from relaxed to restless. Our group, which had initially been enjoying the food and each other's company, started to grow impatient and frustrated. It was clear that the staff was overwhelmed and struggling to keep up with the demands of our large party.

Despite the chaos, the manager did make an effort to come over and apologize for the delays, offering a few complimentary desserts to make up for the inconvenience. However, by that point, many of us had already lost our appetite and were just ready to leave. The desserts, while delicious, were a small consolation for the poor service we had experienced.

As I reflected on the evening, I couldn't help but feel disappointed and frustrated. The food, while tasty, had been overshadowed by the numerous mistakes and delays. The atmosphere, which had initially seemed lacking, had only deteriorated as the night wore on. And the service, which had started out slow, had ultimately fallen apart.

For a restaurant located in a upscale development like CityNorth, I expected a much higher level of quality and attention to detail. Unfortunately, this place fell far short of my expectations. The glowing descriptions on their website and the positive reviews from other diners had led me to believe that this would be a top-notch dining experience. Instead, it was a frustrating and disappointing evening that left a bad taste in my mouth.

In the end, I would not recommend this restaurant to others, at least not until they address the numerous issues with their service and atmosphere. While the food may be good, it's not enough to make up for the poor experience we had. As a host, I felt embarrassed and apologetic to my guests, and I would not want to subject others to the same frustrations. Perhaps with some changes and improvements, this restaurant could live up to its potential and provide a truly enjoyable dining experience. But for now, I'll be taking my business (and my VinVillage events) elsewhere.

Unfortunately, the chocolate flights aren't enough to save this location from its overall shortcomings. The inconsistent food quality and subpar service are major letdowns, especially considering the high standards set by the other Great Danes. It's disappointing to see such a disparity between locations, and I hope they can work to address these issues and bring this spot up to par with its siblings. Until then, I'll stick to visiting the Dane in downtown or Fitchburg.

Saved money and had a much better experience. The prices were transparent and fair, no hidden membership fees. I will never step foot in Camping World again and will be telling all my friends and family to avoid them. Sportsman Warehouse has earned my business and I highly recommend them to anyone looking for outdoor gear. Their honesty and integrity are a breath of fresh air compared to Camping World's deceptive practices.

The portions were generous and the prices were reasonable. Our server was attentive and knowledgeable, making great recommendations. The atmosphere was cozy and inviting, perfect for a night out with friends or a date. We can't wait to come back and try more of their delicious menu items. Overall, this place is a must-visit for anyone looking for great food and a fantastic dining experience in AZ. We're already planning our next visit!

The atmosphere was lacking, and the empty tables made it feel unwelcoming. Our server was friendly, but the slow service didn't help. For a Saturday night, I expected more energy and excitement. Unfortunately, Macayo's has lost its touch, and I wouldn't recommend it to others. The decline in food quality and high prices make it a disappointing experience. Unless they revamp their menu and pricing, I'll take my business elsewhere. It's a shame, as I had fond memories of my previous visit, but this time fell short.

I was extremely disappointed in the lack of communication and follow-through from your shop, especially given the circumstances. While I understood that family emergencies can be unpredictable and overwhelming, it's reasonable to expect some level of communication or effort to resolve the issue after the fact. Instead, I was left to navigate a frustrating and unresponsive system, with no clear resolution in sight. The fact that I had to resort to filing a BBB complaint just to get my money back is a testament to the poor customer service I experienced. It's unfortunate that it took a full year to receive my refund, and even more disappointing that no one from your shop reached out to apologize or explain the delays. As a customer, I expect a certain level of respect and accountability, and it's clear that your shop fell short in this instance. Despite the eventual refund, the experience has left a sour taste, and I would caution others to be aware of the potential for similar issues.

As I look back on my experience with this Pho spot, I am reminded of the warning signs that I chose to ignore. The decline in service and food quality was a gradual one, but it was undeniable. I recall instances where I would arrive at the restaurant, only to be greeted by a hostess who seemed put off by my presence. The servers, who were once so friendly and attentive, began to seem overworked and disinterested. The food, which was once the highlight of my week, started to taste mass-produced and lacking in depth.

I tried to brush off these issues, telling myself that every restaurant has off days. But the problems persisted, and I found myself leaving the restaurant feeling disappointed and unsatisfied more often than not. The health inspections, which I had initially dismissed as a minor setback, began to weigh on my mind. How could a restaurant that was once so meticulous about its food and service allow such lapses in quality control?

Despite my better judgment, I continued to return to the restaurant, hoping that it would somehow magically revert to its former glory. But with each subsequent visit, my disappointment grew. The broth, which was once rich and flavorful, became dull and uninspired. The meat, which was once tender and juicy, became tough and overcooked. It was as if the restaurant had given up on its core values and was simply going through the motions.

My final visit was the last straw. The presence of soy sauce in my Pho was a jarring and unpleasant surprise, and it was then that I knew I had to accept that this relationship was truly over. It's not often that I write scathing reviews, but in this case, I feel that it's necessary to warn others about the decline of this once-beloved Pho spot.

As I close this chapter and move on to better Pho, I am reminded that even the most ardent fans can become disillusioned. It's a hard lesson to learn, but sometimes it's necessary to acknowledge when a relationship has run its course. I hope that the owners of this restaurant will take my feedback to heart and strive to regain their former excellence, but for now, I must bid them adieu.
